title: Trump administration keeps sending contradictory, mixed signals on Iran war
transcription: As American air strikes hammer Iran, the White House remains unable to clearly explain why it decided to attack or how long the war will last. This is not endless, it's not protracted, we're not allowing mission creep. At the Pentagon, the defense secretary would only give vague answers about a timeline, and wouldn't say what it would take to end the war. We will not relent until the enemy is totally and decisively defeated. I think you'll see it's going to be a short-term excursion. President Donald Trump claims it will all be over quickly. He's vowing to fight on to an undisclosed endpoint without saying how long that could take. We could go further, and we're going to go further. The most honest assessments may have come from Israel, America's partner in this war. Israel's foreign minister said there's no sign the fighting is close to over. We are not close there as the president of the United States said yesterday. In Washington, there's a growing sense of unease. Lawmakers left a classified briefing with the White House, clearly alarmed at what they heard and did not hear. We are hearing no logical estimates about when it will be over. It's possible an end is brought about by politics before peace. title: Macron deploys carrier near Cyprus as Europe shows military power
transcription: France declared its presence unmistakably with the French presidential aircraft's arrival on Cyprus and the presence of its frigate and the Charles de Gaulle aircraft carrier nearby. Together with the Greek Prime Minister, President Emmanuel Macron was claiming European primacy in the Eastern Mediterranean. Coming here with the Greek Prime Minister, I want to say that an attack on Cyprus is an attack on Europe. And the defense of Cyprus is a vital issue for your neighbor and friend Greece, but it is also a vital issue for France and for Europe. Greece was the first mover, sending two frigates and four F-16s within 24 hours of a Shahhead type drone striking the British military base at Akrotiri. That has triggered a European response. The leaders of Greece and Cyprus came to deliver messages of solidarity and autonomy, that the security of Cyprus is the security of Europe, and that Europe is capable of providing for its own security. That European presence here is set to grow in the coming days with the arrival of ships from Italy and Spain. Because as the French President said, its credibility is crucial for achieving de-escalation. Both leaders strongly support European defense autonomy, and a new report from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute on Monday revealed that Europe is moving in the right direction. It increased its arms exports by 36% in the last five years, faster than any other region, and now owns 28% of the world's export market for weapons. France with its Rafale fighter jet and missile systems leads European exporters, something showcased here with a French helicopter bought by Cyprus. And a state-of-the-art frigate Greece sent here was just delivered from French shipyards. But the ideological message was equally important. It's an initiative that in practice breathes new life into this article of the treaty. Because if not now, when? If we don't act together in such a crisis, how will we face possible future crises? Now is the time to make it clear that every inch of European territory cannot be violated. And so is the economic message of this high-profile visit, that Europe will keep waterways open for international trade and energy flows. After Russia's war in Ukraine and decades of wars in the Middle East, it is determined to protect its economy from inflation. The subtext of this camaraderie among Europeans is not just that Europe doesn't need the security assistance of the United States, but that the United States has now become part of the problem rather than the solution. John Saropulos, Al Jazeera, Bafos Air Force Base, Cyprus.

title: Removing barriers in cybersecurity: The story behind Amazon’s worldwide HTB CTF event
transcription:
Hi, my name is Pallavi Krishna. I'm a technical program manager, uh working in the application security team in Amazon, India, based out of Bangalore.
Hey, I'm Shahi Sudeer. I'm an offensive security engineer at Amazon, based out of Barcelona, Spain.
The inspiration to host a global CTF competition came from the goal that we wanted to strengthen collaboration with the broader security researcher community. We wanted to collaborate and build a stronger, connected cyber security ecosystem, and also provide a platform for uh external researchers to showcase their skills on real world cybersecurity scenarios.
Within the 48 hours, we got around 1,000 applications. And by the end of registration window, we had 1,500 applicants across the globe. The interest was overwhelming for us.
So, we worked with Hack the Box to create a Jeopardy-style CTF with challenges across web security with code review, AI security, cloud. What this event made it unique, the quality of app-sec challenges we put through and the chance for the top performers who advance the region finals where they could meet Amazon security leaders.
It was really great to see that the top three winners were all in the same room. They had great time and they had wonderful things to share about their experience. Watching the real-time leaderboard during the phase one was so exciting. Seeing people solving the challenges, competing each other. The leaderboard was like changes very quickly, and climbing, the some of them climbing the ranks from all over the world.
In the finals, having a hybrid format across three Amazon offices simultaneously was pretty special.
Initiatives uh like this play a very crucial role in cybersecurity readiness in organizations. It goes beyond theory into continuous learning and hands-on experience. And as cybersecurity threats evolve, managing effectively the human components and the automation of it becomes very crucial. And events like this are core in driving us towards that future.
We did achieve our goals with this competition. We engaged the community in a meaningful way and created a great connection with talented researchers. Uh the participation numbers were strong and the feedback confirmed that people got real value from the event.

title: 1994 Archive: Crossing the Berbice River on the MV Torani - DTV Special Report

title: Tesla Cybertruck Review | The Futuristic Electric Truck That Looks Like It Came From 2050
transcription: The Tesla Cybertruck is one of the most futuristic and talked about electric pickup trucks in the world. Built by Tesla, this vehicle completely changes what people expect from a traditional truck. With its sharp geometric design, stainless steel body, and advanced electric technology, the Cybertruck looks like something straight out of a science fiction movie. One of the most unique things about the Cybertruck is its ultra-hard stainless steel exoskeleton. This special material makes the body extremely durable and resistant to dents and damage. Tesla designed the truck to be both tough and functional, making it suitable for heavy work as well as everyday driving. The Cybertruck is fully electric, which means it produces zero emissions while driving. Depending on the model, it can come with single motor, dual motor, or tri motor electric powertrains. The top version is incredibly powerful and can accelerate from 0 to 60 miles per hour in about 2.6 seconds, which is faster than many sports cars. Another impressive feature of the Cybertruck is its long driving range. The high performance version can travel up to around 500 miles on a single charge, making it one of the longest range electric trucks available. This makes it practical for long trips, work sites, and daily use. Inside the cabin, the Cybertruck offers a minimalist and modern interior. It features a large central touchscreen that controls most of the vehicle's functions, including navigation, entertainment, and climate settings. The spacious cabin can comfortably seat up to six passengers, making it both a family vehicle and a powerful work truck. The truck also offers strong towing and payload capabilities. It can tow up to about 14,000 pounds and carry heavy cargo in its large rear bed, which Tesla calls the vault. The bed also includes a powered cover to protect cargo and improve aerodynamics. In terms of technology, the Cybertruck comes equipped with Tesla's advanced driver assistance features. This includes autopilot, which can help with steering, acceleration, and braking on highways. Future updates may also enable more advanced self-driving capabilities through software updates. Overall, the Tesla Cybertruck represents a bold step into the future of electric trucks. With its unique design, powerful performance, long range and advanced technology, it stands out as one of the most innovative vehicles Tesla has ever created.

title: Anthropic Sues U.S. Government After Pentagon Calls It a “Security Risk” | The AI War Begins
transcription: Imagine building one of the most advanced artificial intelligence systems in the world, and then suddenly being labeled a national security risk by your own government. This is exactly what's happening right now between Anthropic and the United States Department of Defense. But what exactly happened? Anthropic is one of the fastest growing AI companies in the world, and it created the AI assistant Claude, a powerful system designed to compete with the most advanced AI models available today. However, the company has always taken a strong position on one important issue, how its AI should be used. So what is the problem between Anthropic and the US government? The conflict reportedly started when Anthropic refused to allow certain uses of its AI technology. For example, the company says its systems should not be used for fully autonomous weapons, and it also rejects large-scale domestic surveillance applications. But why would that create such a big conflict? Because advanced AI has become extremely valuable for military and defense applications. Governments around the world are racing to integrate artificial intelligence into their security systems, and that brings us to the most surprising part of the story. What did the Pentagon actually do? The US Department of Defense labeled Anthropic as a supply chain risk. This designation is very serious. It can effectively prevent a company from working with US defense agencies and government systems. In fact, reports say federal agencies were instructed to begin phasing out Anthropic technology from their networks. So, how did the company respond? Anthropic strongly rejected the decision and argued that the move is unfair and unjustified. According to the company, the government is punishing them for refusing to weaken safety protections on how their AI can be used. Because of that, Anthropic has now taken the fight to court. The company is asking a federal judge to overturn the Pentagon's decision. And this raises an even bigger question. What makes this case so important? If the lawsuit moves forward, it could become one of the first major legal battles between an AI developer and the US government. And the outcome may shape the future of artificial intelligence. So the real question is this, who should control powerful AI systems? The governments that want to use them, or the companies that build them? Let me know what you think in the comments. And follow Creations Tech for more stories about the technologies shaping our future.

title: LAFD: Major Emergency Structure Fire in Hollywood Hills | March 9, 2026
transcription: The Los Angeles Fire Department responded to a structure fire in the Hollywood Hills area on St. Ives Drive involving a four-story hillside home. More than 100 firefighters with mutual aid assistance from Los Angeles County Fire and the Beverly Hills Fire Department working together to bring the fire under control in about 42 minutes. The fire was confined to the roof of the home and LAFD Air units were overhead monitoring for ember cast to ensure there was no spread into the surrounding brush. The occupants were inside the home when the fire started but were able to safely evacuate and were not injured. title: Protesters Rally at WV Capitol Against Morrisey’s ICE Pact
transcription: And convoys from all across West Virginia rolled into Charleston today for a rally at the State Capitol. Supporters say they want state leaders to stop helping federal ICE officers, instead, focus on protecting their own communities. Our Bethany Jarrell has more from the capital. Here at the state capital where supporters from across West Virginia are gathering to send a message to Governor Patrick Morrisey. They're calling on lawmakers to stop cooperating with federal immigration enforcement, saying all people deserve due process. in the first place. This is not just policy failure, this is false hope. And it undermines its very values we claim to stand for. The truth is, the people being targeted are often workers, parents and neighbors. People who came here looking for the same thing our ancestors did, which is a better life. Last year, Governor Patrick Morrisey signed an agreement with ICE, bringing West Virginia law enforcement into the 287G program. This allowed officers to help identify and detain people suspected of violating immigration law. We're here today because Governor Morrisey has issued a order that has our state police and our county police helping the federal government help Ice go into communities when they should be in our own communities taking care of us. In January, ICE said more than 650 people were arrested in a statewide operation with help from local law enforcement. Protesters say concerns about enforcement tactics and due process are driving today's rally. If you interact with anybody who's had any experience in long-term law enforcement, nobody would say that their agents should be masked, that they should just be able to pull people up without due process to be able to treat them violently. This is a blemish on basic law enforcement, what's happening right now. Some protesters point to West Virginia's declining population, saying the current system targets the wrong people, including immigrants who contribute to communities across the state. You know, these people that are doing valuable work and are just decent human beings trying to live their life. Why why would we want to drive them away? Um, so I'm I'm just really interested in trying to help other people that live here in West Virginia that maybe don't understand or don't have any experience with immigration or immigrants to understand a little bit better what that value is and why this is maybe not the best way what we're doing right now. Many at the rally say they support immigration enforcement, but believe it should focus on serious crimes and follow due process. We believe in due process, accountability, and human dignity. And we're going to keep fighting for it. Now organizers say rallies like this are meant to push state leaders to reconsider the state's approach to immigration enforcement. And the only way to fix it is for the people to stand up, rise up and make it happen. Reporting in Charleston, Bethany Jarrell, Eyewitness News.

title: Alphabet Offers Sundar Pichai $692 Million Pay Package; Amazon, Microsoft, Google Back Claude
transcription: It has been quite a weekend in the world of AI. Let's start with Alphabet. The company has awarded CEO Sundar Pichai a pay package worth up to $692 million. But the structure of that compensation is what stands out. A large portion of it is tied not to Alphabet's overall stock performance, but to whether its autonomous ventures, Waymo and Wing, increase the value over the next three years. That is about $392 million of the total pay package. Now, if those businesses fail to grow, the payout does not materialize in the same way, which means the message from Alphabet's board is pretty clear. Autonomy and AI-driven infrastructure are no longer experimental projects, but quite central to the company's long-term strategy. Defense AI is also accelerating. Shares of Palantir technologies rose up to 15% in the week gone by as tensions around the Iran conflict rose. Palantir's Maven smart system is already embedded within US military operations and is designed to process real-time sensor and operational data to support battlefield decisions. At the same time, tensions between AI companies and the Pentagon are becoming more and more visible. After the US Department of Defense labeled Anthropic a potential supply chain risk, major cloud providers including Amazon, Microsoft, and Google moved to reassure customers that Anthropic's Claude model will continue to be available for enterprise workloads. Meanwhile, XAI led by Elon Musk has secured a deal to deploy its Grock model inside classified US defense systems in place of Claude. But Grock is also under scrutiny after generating racist content and false claims about the Hillsborough disaster, triggering investigations by regulators across UK, EU, and California. Now, there are also developments at Open AI. CEO Sam Altman says that the company has again delayed the launch of Chat GPT's planned adult mode, which would allow verified users to access explicit content. Open AI says it is prioritizing improvements to intelligence, personality, and proactive capabilities before introducing this feature. And from India, a development that could prove strategically significant. Sarvam AI has launched two open weight models. These are trained on Indian languages. One has 30 billion parameters and the other 105 billion. Now, the larger model claims benchmark performance comparable to Deepseek's R1 model despite using far fewer parameters. Then there's a US company called Target Hospitality. This is the same company that runs the ICE detention facilities in the US and has now signed more more than $130 million in contracts to build temporary worker housing for laborers constructing new AI data centers in rural Texas. It is a sign that AI race is now driving a massive physical build out involving land, power, labor, and infrastructure across multiple regions.

title: Microsoft Agent 365 - The control plane for AI agents
transcription: Today you're being asked to move faster than ever. and agents are quickly becoming the way work gets done. But when agents start multiplying, IT and security inherit a new challenge. How do you innovate without creating risk, silos, or a patchwork of tools? That's where Agent 365 comes in. The enterprise control plane for managing all of your organization's agents securely at scale. Because it's integrated directly into the Microsoft 365 admin center, you manage agents in one unified place, right alongside the day-to-day work of managing users, apps, and policies. Agent 365 shows how agents connect to each other, no matter where it was built or what platform it runs on. There's clear visibility into security, adoption, operational health, and business impact. The same identity and access system you use for people extends to agents. Then, you can focus attention where it matters most. Built-in risk signals help flag agents that need review. So your team can investigate quickly and, when necessary, lock access to sensitive resources. Agent 365 also helps you understand how agents connect to each other. So you can spot dependencies, performance bottlenecks, and potential security gaps before they become incidents. When new agents are introduced, bring them in safely with consistent guardrails for access, policy, permissions, and approvals to the users who need them most. Agent 365 is more than a way to manage agents. It gives you a secure, unified foundation to scale them across your business, using the IT, security, and governance controls from Microsoft that you already trust.

title: Two charged with terrorism after homemade bomb thrown in New York
transcription: Two men accused of igniting homemade bombs at a chaotic anti-Islam protest outside the New York City Mayor's Mansion were charged on Monday with federal terrorism-related crimes. That's according to court records that said 18-year-old Amir Balat and 19-year-old Ibrahim Kayumi told police they were inspired by Islamic State, the Islamist militant group. The two young men are accused of traveling from Pennsylvania with dangerous improvised explosive devices to Manhattan on Saturday. That's when a small group of far right activists had planned the anti-Muslim rally outside Gracie Mansion against Zoran Momdani, New York City's first Muslim mayor. On Monday, Momdani condemned the two men's attempt to carry out an attack at the rally. Anti-Muslim bigotry is nothing new to me, nor is it anything new for the 1 million or so Muslim New Yorkers who know this city as our home. While I found this protest appalling, I will not waver in my belief that it should be allowed to happen. Ours is a free society where the right to peaceful protest is sacred. Momdani and his wife were not at home at the time of Saturday's incident. Police were able to intercept the explosive devices, which were duct tape jars containing screws and bolts in an explosive substance. No one was hurt. Police said it was the first time an improvised bomb was deployed in New York City in nearly a decade. According to a complaint filed by the US Attorney's office in Manhattan, Balat and Kaimi are each charged with five federal crimes, including use of a weapon of mass destruction and three charges related to the illegal possession or transportation of explosives.

title: Keir Starmer discusses Iran war with Donald Trump during call
transcription:
UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has spoken on the phone with the US President Donald Trump for the first time since the outbreak of war in the Middle East. Amanda Akass reports.
We're told the phone call lasted around 20 minutes. We do have a read out of that conversation. It never get goes into a lot of detail, but it gives a flavor of the key topics. So we're told they began by discussing the latest situation in the Middle East and the military cooperation between the UK and US through the use of RAF bases in support of the collective self-defense of partners in the region. The Prime Minister also shared his heartfelt condolences with President Trump and the American people following the deaths of six US soldiers. They looked forward to speaking again soon. Um, now what's interesting, I think is that this is much more of a kind of typical readout that we normally get, ending with these kind of warm words about speaking again soon, compared to what happened uh a week ago on the first day of the strikes when we were basically just told they discussed the Middle East and there was no kind of formal explanation of what was said. Now, clearly, we now know that Donald Trump was exceedingly angry, incandescent, it seems, with Sir Kier Starmer for not giving permission for the US to use UK military bases to launch those initial strikes. Um, even though he has softened that position and allowing US uh jets to use UK bases for defensive activities now. We're seeing that beginning uh this weekend. Um, the rest of the week has been full of insults frankly flying across the Atlantic with Donald Trump saying that Sir Kier Starmer is no Winston Churchill, saying he's disappointed with the UK position. And even Sir Kier Starmer making it quite clear that he he's opposed to the to the way the strikes happened, talking about his support for international law, and the fact that his government doesn't support regime change from the skies. And then last night, this really blistering message on Truth Social from Donald Trump, talking about our former great ally and saying we don't need people who only join us in our wars once we've already won. Um so clearly the special relationship is in a very delicate state. So Downing Street will be pleased that this call happened at all.

title: Oppo Watch X3 Smartwatch | First Look & Launch Date!
transcription: Oppo appears to be positioning the Watch X3 as a premium, tough-built smartwatch rather than chasing the ultra-thin trend that others are leaning into right now. A titanium alloy bezel and sapphire crystal display protection are both on the list, which would put the Watch X3 in premium territory. Weight is expected to come in around 68 grams with color options spanning black, silver, titanium, and orange. The design sticks with the round form factor used on the Watch X2 and there's a rotating crown alongside a second side button for hardware navigation. That combination of touch and physical controls has become a signature of the Watch X line. On the display side, a 1.5-inch LTPO AMOLED panel is. Its peak brightness is at around 2,200 nits. Internally, the Watch X3 is to carry a dual-chip setup, which Oppo has used before to balance performance with power efficiency. The idea is that a low-power co-processor handles background tasks and standby, keeping the main chip free for heavier lifting. RAM and storage are expected to land at 2 gigabytes and 32 gigabytes respectively. The battery capacity is at 632 milliamp hours, which is on the larger end for a Wear OS device. The Watch X2 already stood out for its endurance, so a bigger cell in the X3 would only strengthen that reputation. Software is Wear OS 6, based on Android 16, bringing Google Maps, Wallet, and Play Store access along with it. Connectivity should cover LTE with eSIM, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and NFC for payments. Health features are expected to include heart rate, sleep tracking, GPS, and a range of sports modes with ECG. The Watch X3 looks more like an evolution of the Watch X2 than a fresh start. Oppo seems to be taking what already worked and turning up the dial in a few specific areas. For now, the March 17th date is the one to watch.

title: Trump, Starmer discuss Iran, after US says no need for UK help
transcription: Iran. US President Donald Trump has dismissed Britain's consideration of sending aircraft carriers to the Middle East, saying the United States does not need them to win the war with Iran. We don't need them. It's not the right time. It would have been nice to have had them two weeks ago. Trump was speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One after Britain's Defense Ministry said on Saturday, it was preparing the Prince of Wales aircraft carrier for possible deployment. But no final decision had been taken about whether to send it to the Middle East, a British official said. In response, Trump posted on social media that he quote, will remember the lack of British support during the conflict with Iran. The President has repeatedly criticized Britain's Prime Minister Kier Starmer over his stance on the war. He suggested this week that Starmer helped ruin the country's historically close ties after London blocked initial US use of British bases to attack Iran. Starmer has defended that decision saying he needed to be satisfied that any military action was legal and well-planned. He later granted US forces permission to use British bases for what he called limited and defensive strikes to weaken Tehran's capabilities. On Sunday, Starmer's office said the pair had spoken on Iran as two US Air Force planes arrived at an airbase in England. The Prime Minister's office released a statement saying the use of Royal Air Force bases was discussed, quote, in support of the collective self-defense of partners in the region. Starmer's office did not address Trump's criticisms, but said the Prime Minister offered his condolences over the deaths of six US soldiers killed in the conflict.

title: Terrorism task force investigating after 'suspicious devices' thrown outside NYC mayor's home
transcription: New details tonight after a suspicious smoking device was thrown during dueling protests outside the official New York City Mayor's residence. The NYPD Commissioner shared this photo showing police running toward the device. Investigators say the initial protest called Stop the Islamic Takeover of New York was organized by a right-wing group. Now, Mayor Zoran Mamdani is Muslim. We're now learning two counter-protesters are connected to two devices found at the scene containing metal fuses and metal. The commissioner says an 18-year-old counter-protester ignited one of the devices and threw it into the protest area where it landed near police officers. He then allegedly retrieved a second device from another 19-year-old counter-protester and lit it and dropped it on the street. Both individuals were then arrested. The devices, which were a bit smaller than a football, appear to be a jar wrapped in black tape, importantly, with nuts, bolts, and screws along with a hobby fuse that could be lit. Witnesses reported seeing flames and smoke as it traveled through the air before it struck a barrier and extinguished itself a few feet from police officers. Police say a total of six people were arrested including a demonstrator from the far right group who used pepper spray on a counter protester. Mayor Zoran Mamdani's press secretary released a statement saying in part, the mayor and the first lady are both safe, though the events are a stark reminder of the threats they both face regularly.

transcription: Hi Lewis. Are you sorry? Yeah, yeah, no problem. Thank you. Um, are you still smiling? You were smiling earlier in the weekend. Are you still smiling today after that first day? Yeah. Yeah, it was not the best qualifying, but um, I felt solid all weekend. I've been really, really happy in the car and um, feeling super motivated and I think um, in Q2, Q1 was up until Q1, end of Q1 on the medium tire was feeling great. I was obviously, it was third or fourth with just the medium tire, so it was feeling solid. and then when we got into Q2, we had some problems with the with the engine and the deployment and it kind of then threw a bunch of spanners in the mix and we really struggled then to just just execute and get the best out of it after that. Um, so I think on a if things hadn't been an issue, I think we probably could have been fighting for third, third or fourth. So, um I don't think we can keep up, catch, get anywhere in Mercedes, but um, still, lots of work to to progress to be made. Are you surprised by that gap to Mercedes and do you think you can do you think you can take advantage at the start tomorrow? because your starts seem to have been phenomenal on the practices we've seen. I think what's clear is that they didn't show the the engine power through any of the practice because they, you know, there's the whole talk of compression ratio and they've obviously done a really solid job with their engine, which we have as well, but it would be interesting to I I'm trying to I want to understand why it's you know, it's like two tens or more just just through power per sector. title: Lewis Hamilton Urges Africa to ‘Take Back’ Its Future in Powerful Speech
transcription: Lewis Hamilton calls for Africa to take it back as F1 return debate heats up. Seven-time Formula 1 World Champion Lewis Hamilton has made headlines after calling on African nations to take Africa back from former colonial powers, including France, Spain, Portugal, and Britain. Hamilton made the comments while responding to a South African journalist who asked about Formula 1's long-awaited return to the continent. The sport has not held a race in Africa since the 1993 South African Grand Prix at Kyalami. The British racing icon revealed he has been pushing for years to bring Formula 1 back to Africa and says he won't retire until it happens. I've been fighting for the past six, seven years to get the sport back there. Hamilton said, making it clear that a race on African soil is a personal mission for him. Opening up about his heritage, Hamilton added, I'm half African. I've got roots from Benin, Senegal, Nigeria. It's something I'm really proud of. He went on to speak passionately about the continent's future, saying he believes Africa has the potential to be the greatest and most powerful place in the world because of its vast natural resources. However, he also expressed frustration about foreign influence over African economies and leadership structures. I don't like that the rest of the world owns so much of it and takes so much from it and no one speaks about it, he said. I'm really looking forward to hoping that the people running those different countries unite and take Africa back from the French, from the Spanish, from the Portuguese and the British. Hamilton has frequently visited Africa in recent years. During his 2024 mid-season break, he spent significant time in Senegal, describing the trip as heavy but deeply meaningful. He said it was important to learn history and honor the people and cultures his family roots trace back to. Beyond his activism, Hamilton is also preparing for the start of a new Formula 1 season, with the opening race set to take place in Australia this weekend. He marked race week with a shirtless Instagram post captioned, Race week, I'm ready. Off the track, Hamilton has also been making headlines for his personal life. Reports suggest he has recently been spending time with reality TV star Kim Kardashian. The pair were reportedly seen together at an exclusive desert destination near the Colorado River, close to the ultra-private Amangiri resort. The luxury hideaway is known for attracting high-profile celebrities seeking privacy with suites costing thousands of dollars per night. According to reports, Hamilton and Kardashian were spotted taking a cozy selfie before leaving in a black SUV. The sighting follows their joint public appearance at the Super Bowl last month, fueling speculation that their relationship may be getting serious. As the new F1 season begins, Hamilton is once again in the spotlight, not just for his racing ambitions, but for his outspoken views on heritage, global politics, and representation in sport. Whether it's campaigning for Formula One's return to Africa or navigating high-profile romance rumors, Lewis Hamilton continues to make an impact both on and off the track.

title: U.S.-Spain military dispute, global tariffs rise to 15%, major blackout in Cuba, 87 bodies recovered
transcription: This is the world now, bringing you everything you need to know from around the globe. The Spanish government has denied White House claims that Madrid agreed to cooperate with US military operations in the Middle East. Spanish Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Alvarez on Wednesday rejected White House statements that Madrid had agreed to support US strikes against Iran. The denial follows President Trump's threat on Tuesday to cut off all trade after Spain barred the US from using joint military bases for its attacks on Iran. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez also on Wednesday reaffirmed his no to the war policy, describing the conflict in Iran as quote Russian roulette with millions of lives. A US submarine on Wednesday sank the Iranian frigate Iris Denna in the Indian Ocean off the coast of Sri Lanka. US Defense Secretary Pete Heth confirmed the US Navy conducted the strike against the vessel in international waters. Sri Lankan military rescuers recovered 87 bodies from the site and treated 32 survivors at the hospital in the port city of Gaul. The Iranian ship was traveling from India to Iran following a multilateral naval exercise in the Bay of Bengal. Sri Lankan authorities are continuing search and rescue operations for approximately 60 missing crew members. Treasury Secretary Scott Beson on Wednesday confirmed the US will raise the global import tariff rate to 15% this week. That's an increase from the current 10% tariffs. The administration is implementing the hike under section 122 of the 1974 Trade Act. It is a 150-day temporary measure, but Beson told CNBC that during that time, the government will conduct studies for more permanent tariffs. That measure was brought in after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's previous tariffs. A total power failure on Wednesday disconnected the Cuban National electric grid, leaving most of the island without electricity. The state electric utility UNE attributed the blackout to an unexpected outage caused by a boiler leak at the Antonio Gutirrez's thermoelectric plant. The energy ministry confirmed that the outage halted water services, transportation, and state media broadcasts across Havana and western provinces of Cuba. To Dehan, Adilang News.

The more affordable Galaxy A37 will also feature five color choices, white, charcoal, gray green, lavender and navy. From a design perspective, the Galaxy A57 has slimmer bezels compared to the A37. Both smartphones follow a similar design language, featuring buttons placed on the right side, an oval-shaped camera module at the back, and a glass back panel. A new official leak from the European Union's Iprel database, first reported by Newarmobil, reveals key details about the upcoming Samsung Galaxy A37 and Samsung Galaxy A57. Both phones have secured an A energy efficiency rating and are rated for up to 53 hours A37 and 52 hours A57 of battery life on a single charge, a major improvement over the previous generation. The listing also shows 1,200 charge cycles for battery longevity, which appears lower than last year, but is likely due to updated EU testing standards rather than a drop in quality. In terms of durability, both devices are expected to feature an IP68 rating, upgrading from IP67. This means better protection against dust and water, allowing submersion in up to 1.5 m of water for 30 minutes. The A57 also reportedly gets a higher drop resistance grade than the A37, suggesting stronger build materials. Both smartphones are expected to launch in March 2026.

title: Hundreds rally against restrictions on public employee unions in Florida
transcription: At Florida's Capital this afternoon, a Senate committee making a major change to a controversial bill that puts more restrictions on public employee labor unions. Our Capital Bureau reporter Cody Butler tells us this will create another showdown between the House and Senate. The legislature's been passing laws over the last several years, putting more restrictions on labor unions across the state and this year is no different. hundreds of thousands across the state are going to lose their rights, death by a thousand bureaucratic paper cuts should this legislation pass. Please vote no. And I stand in strong opposition of this bill. After one, more than 100 electricians, bus drivers, teachers, sanitation workers, and other public employees urged senators Monday to stop putting more restrictions on labor unions across the state. Dozens of them rallied before the Senate Fiscal Policy meeting concerned that these changes could do more harm. We do not need a piece of legislation like Senate Bill 1296 that is going to harm us even further than we already are and make it harder than it already is to continue doing the job. The committee made changes to Senate Bill 1296 while still building off public employee union requirements implemented a couple years ago. The changes require unions to have 20% of their members vote on ratification and recertification, and then 60% to pass. The bill also limits when they can take paid leave to advocate for union issues. Polk County teacher Laura Allgood says this bill could make life more difficult for unions and their members. I love teaching and I love my students and I want to continue to do this job and I don't want to do it any harder than it already is now. And I urge you, please vote no. It's important to have a safeguard in here. I think a simple majority is like, it's, it it feels common sense to me. Senator Jonathan Martin is carrying the bill. He says it's needed to make sure more people have the right to work. in certifying this bargaining group, you're requiring every other person out there who's in that group to keep their mouth shut. They don't have the ability to go and negotiate their own um, their own salary, their own benefits. The house has a similar bill ready for a vote, but it doesn't include the changes made in the Senate on Monday. Al says lawmakers should be focusing on several other issues instead. my students, the families, the things that I see because they can't make a living. I see we have out of control discipline. We have so many things going on in our school. We need to be focusing on that. Now if this does become law, there are likely to be legal challenges. A legislative staff analysis says that provisions in this bill could be unconstitutional. At the Florida State Capitol, I'm Cody Butler reporting.

title: Whaling History | Industrial Era & Whale Oil (Raw Footage) | Warrnambool fun
transcription: The roar of the machines of the Industrial Revolution signaled momentous changes. The steam-driven machines of the Victorian era transformed the world. Automation created entirely new industries that allowed factories to produce goods on an unimaginable scale. Goods were traded around the world, and in return, exotic goods from the far corners of the globe were imported. If you were part of the middle class, it was a time of plenty and a cornucopia of goods from all over the world could be purchased at one of the latest innovations, the department store. In the glittering surrounding of Harrod's, can be found practically anything from almost anywhere in the world. Ivory goods from the Orient, ebony from darkest Africa, sandwich glass from Massachusetts, coffee from Brazil, porcelain from the Orient. Of all the products available to the well-to-do in the Victorian age, one of the most indispensable was whale oil. Its superior lubricating qualities made whale oil the ideal product to keep industrial steam engines operating. But whale oil was also used on the domestic front. Whale oil lamps lit up the homes of the wealthy and fashionable. It provided a brighter light than other animal fats available and produced far less smoke. Whale oil was extensively used in toiletries, cosmetics, and soaps. While whale oil was highly prized, whale bone too was a much sought-after product. In many ways, whale bone was the plastic of its day. It was strong and flexible and could be put to numerous uses. Whalebone was used to make buggy whips, as well as the springs on which the carriages rode. It was used to make brushes, combs, the ribs for parasols and umbrellas, and fishing rods. But it was in women's fashion that whalebone made the greatest impression. To complete the ensemble, voluminous skirts supported by hoops of whalebone were all the rage in fashionable society. Whalebone and oil were luxury products, but the fashions and technology of the day meant there was a ready market willing to pay a premium for them.

What you need to understand is that a pixel is basically a tiny light collector that turns light into electrons. The brighter your subject, the more electrons. But there's a limit, the full well capacity of your pixels. So, when there's a really bright highlight like this fire, I'll just take a quick shot on the iPhone first. Can you see this? It's producing more electrons than the pixels in this camera can hold. So, there is a bunch of information lost. The highlights just become these pure white patches with no detail. This is also known as clipping. And so that is where Lofic comes in, which stands for Lateral Overflow Integration Capacitor. I wouldn't worry too much about that name, but the key word in it is overflow. It essentially means that each pixel here has an entire extra bucket to be able to capture that light information so that it's not lost. Which is why if we take the exact same shot on this now, can you see how compared to that last shot, a lot more of the detail in the fire is still visible, which is not a complete surprise given that this thing has over six times the full well capacity of the previous Xiaomi. Most phones will try to get around their limitations here by taking multiple shots at various different exposures and then fusing them together. But that only really works with photos, and if the subject is moving a lot, you're going to get motion blur. The second unique thing going on with the 17 Ultra is with this camera. This is a 200 megapixel telephoto camera with mechanical optical zoom. Very reminiscent of a DSLR zoom lens. See, the issue that you have almost definitely run into when using your phone is, yes, the individual cameras may be higher resolution, but they almost always have fixed lenses and therefore fixed focal lengths. Meaning that as soon as you start tweaking the magnification, even slightly, your phone might suddenly have to jump to using one of its other cameras while then applying a bunch of digital zoom so the quality drops fast. title: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra - Unboxing! (Sky Blue)
transcription: Yes, this is the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. And the crazy part, the official launch hasn't even happened yet, but somehow it's already right here in our hands. Today, you're seeing it before most of the world does. The unit I'm holding is sky blue with 512 gigabytes of storage. It also comes in black, white, and purple. And the second you pick it up, you feel it. Something is different. It's slimmer now, just 7.9 mm compared to 8.2 before. On paper, that sounds tiny. In your hand, it feels lighter, cleaner, more refined. It feels expensive. From the front, it looks familiar, classic Ultra. But flip it over and the new camera rings catch your eye. They're smoother, more rounded, more elegant. It's a subtle redesign, but it makes the entire phone look sharper and more polished. The S Pen is still here, of course, slightly reshaped so it flows better with the curved frame. Bluetooth features are still missing, but there's a small detail that feels surprisingly satisfying. The tip now matches the color of the phone. It's subtle, but it feels intentional. Under the hood, it's powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. Right now, this is one of the most powerful processors available. Everything reacts instantly. Apps open without hesitation, animations glide, it feels effortless. The 6.9-inch AMOLED M14 display is stunning, bright, crisp, incredibly vibrant. But the real surprise is the new privacy display mode. Turn it on and side angles become harder to read. Perfect for flights, cafes, crowded spaces. And when you don't need it, you switch it off in seconds. Battery capacity stays at 5,000 mA per hour. Samsung claims up to 31 hours of video playback. Charging has improved too, up to 65 W. It can reach 75% in about 30 minutes. That's fast enough to change how you use your day. The camera system is still serious. 200 MP main sensor, 50 MP ultrawide, 50 MP telephoto, 12 MP front camera. But this year, it's not just about hardware, it's about artificial intelligence. Smarter zoom, better detail, cleaner night shots, more natural processing. So now the real question, is it worth upgrading? If you're chasing top-tier performance, a more refined design, and smarter features powered by artificial intelligence, the Galaxy S26 Ultra makes a very strong argument.

As far as the specifications are concerned, it is almost confirmed by now that the Nothing phone 4A has the Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 chipset. It is also said that this time there is UFS 3.1 storage, which if true will be a big upgrade from the UFS 2.2 storage in the last year's phone 3A. Personally, I really like the design of the Nothing phone 4A and it is much, much better than what we got with the Nothing phone 3 last year. title: Far-Right Britain First Protest in Manchester Ends in Clashes and Arrests | SKY 522
transcription:
Hello, I'm Sanya for TM News English. Tensions flared in Manchester City Centre today as far-right demonstrators clashed with counter-protesters, leading to multiple arrests and a major police operation. Let's see the report.
Hundreds of far-right demonstrators clashed with larger groups of counter-protesters in Manchester city centre during a tense standoff that led to multiple arrests. Supporters of Britain First gathered on Saturday for an anti-Islam march, chanting anti-immigration slogans beneath a city centre underpass as Union Jacks fluttered overhead. Some protesters appeared to be under the influence of alcohol as they criticized migrants and Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer. A counter-demonstration, organized by anti-fascist groups, drew a significantly larger crowd a few streets away. Protesters carried anti-racist placards and flags, including Palestinian flags, and accused Britain First of promoting racist and divisive views. As the two marches converged, tensions escalated. Protesters traded insults and police struggled to keep the groups apart. Some Britain First supporters reportedly prodded counter-protesters with flagpoles while others slipped through police lines. Officers described the operation as particularly challenging, with routes changing and additional events in the city stretching resources. Greater Manchester Police said nine men were arrested on suspicion of offences including assaulting an emergency worker, public order offences, breach of the peace and breaching a dispersal notice. A dispersal order was put in place across the city centre until 8 p.m., giving officers powers to remove individuals from the area. Assistant Chief Constable Rick Jackson said additional officers, including mounted and dog units, were deployed to support peaceful protest while minimizing disruption to the wider public.

title: Memo shows LAFD tried to 'protect' Mayor Bass ahead of Palisades after-action report
transcription: Eyewitness News has uncovered a confidential memo that shows how the LA Fire Department tried to shield Mayor Karen Bass after the Palisades fire. It appears the department was concerned about potential harm to its and the mayor's reputation over the city's handling of that deadly wildfire. Eyewitness News reporter Michelle Fischer, live in our newsroom now with a closer look at that memo. Michelle? Mark, this all comes after the LA Times broke a story several weeks ago claiming the Palisades fire after-action report was watered down. And since our Seven on Your Side investigative team has been looking into that claim. Tonight, the new confidential memo shedding some more insight into how the LA Fire Department sought to get ahead of the fallout that was anticipated from the after-action report. Through a public records request, the Seven on your Side Investigates team obtained this internal memo from last October. The strategic response plan shows the LAFD working with public relations consultants to mitigate concern about how the Palisades fire after-action report could impact the reputation of the mayor and the fire department. The memo saying, quote, it's our goal to prepare and protect Mayor Bass, the city and the LAFD from reputational harm associated with the upcoming public release of its after-action report through a comprehensive strategy that includes risk assessment, proactive and reactive communications and crisis response. The memo goes on to detail how the department wanted to have pre-release meetings with the LAFD Fire Commission and certain council members to, quote, minimize tough Q&A and secure alliance ahead of the city council public meeting. Tonight, Mayor Bass's office in a statement saying, quote, it's important to note that the fire department hired this consultant, not the mayor's office. And consultants write all sorts of memos promising to save the world. LAFD incorporated this consultant into its team, so of course, and appropriately, the mayor's office engaged with that team. Mayor Bass removed the previous fire chief over the chief's refusal to do an after-action report and for failure to pre-deploy. The notion that the mayor then took a U-turn and watered down a report that justified her removal of the chief and her public criticisms of pre-deployment failures is just bonkers. And ABC 7 did also reach out to the LAFD for comment on this latest memo, but so far, we have not yet heard back tonight. Reporting live in the news room, I'm Michelle Fisher, ABC 7 Eyewitness News. Michelle Fisher, thank you.

title: Malibu Sues State of California, City of Los Angeles Over Palisades Fire
transcription:
The city of Malibu is suing the state of California and city of Los Angeles over the Palisades fire. The lawsuit claims that government failures worsened the destruction. NTD's Christina Corona tells us more.
The city of Malibu is seeking accountability months after the Palisades fire tore through the community. It's asking for damages from the state of California as well as several state, county, and local agencies. In a 66-page complaint, Malibu says the wildfire destroyed more than 700 homes and dozens of businesses, leaving burn scars along the Pacific Coast Highway and damaging areas like Carbon Beach. City leaders say Malibu's entire character changed after the blaze burned down parts of the beachside community. The complaint says the fire was not an act of nature, but a result of what the city calls unlawful conduct and failures in inspection and emergency preparedness. The lawsuit claims officials prioritized protecting rare and environmentally sensitive plants over clearing hazardous vegetation near the site of the earlier Lochman fire, a burn area that allegedly reignited just days later. The city argues that state employees hindered firefighters' efforts to cut dry brush and remove fuel, even though hotspots and active burn areas were still visible. The lawsuit seeks to recover financial losses, including costs of emergency response, infrastructure repairs, environmental restoration, and lost revenue from tourism and local businesses. Malibu Mayor Bruce Silverstein says the decision to sue was not made lightly, adding that the city has a duty to protect residents and taxpayers while continuing to work with regional partners. The state of California and the city of Los Angeles have not yet commented on the lawsuit. Christina Corona, NTD News.

title: Deadly Floods in Indonesia: Jakarta Targets Firms Over Deforestation | WION
transcription: Now deadly flooding in Indonesia has triggered sweeping government action against companies who are accused of worsening the disaster through deforestation. Permits have been revoked, lawsuits filed, and state takeovers threatened. But environmentalists warn the response may fall short and could even put fragile ecosystems at greater risk. After last year's catastrophic floods and landslides in Sumatra that killed more than a thousand people, officials under President Prabowo Subianto acknowledged that deforestation and overdevelopment played a major role in amplifying the disaster. Years of mining, plantation expansion, and forest fires have stripped vast stretches of rainforest across Sumatra, removing trees that once absorbed heavy rainfall and stabilized soil on steep hillsides. Dozens of companies have had their permits revoked, and the government plans to hand management of roughly 1 million hectares of land to a state enterprise. Initially, authorities indicated that the move would include the Martabe gold mine in the ecologically sensitive Batang Toru region, and conservationists have long accused the site of environmental damage. Officials now say that they are still reviewing possible violations, but critics note there's no indication development will halt in Batang Toru. Now, Batang Toru is home to the world's rarest great ape, the Tapanuli orangutan. Fewer than 800 were believed to exist in the wild before the floods. Using satellite data, experts estimate nearly 60 orangutans may have died in what they described as an extinction-level event for the species. Now, between 2001 and 2004, Sumatra lost 4.4 million hectares of forest. That's an area larger than Switzerland, making its landscapes increasingly vulnerable to landslides and flash flooding. Environmental groups warn that transferring land to state control does not guarantee better environmental practices. They say the government has yet to outline clear plans for forest recovery or long-term remediation. Now, lawsuits are seeking nearly $300 million from six companies, some funds earmarked for environmental repair. Experts argue far greater investment will be needed, and more firms may share responsibility.

title: Mark Zuckerberg takes the stand in landmark trial over social media addiction claims
transcription: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg was grilled for nearly 8 hours in a landmark trial over claims that Instagram is designed to be addictive for kids and teens. During the sometimes tense exchanges in a Los Angeles courtroom, Zuckerberg defended the app's restrictions which ban users under 13, but he acknowledged, I always wish we could have gotten there sooner. and he pointed to challenges, saying the company has acknowledged for a while that people get around the age restrictions. The lawsuit was brought by a now 20-year-old woman known as Kelly, who says she started using the app when she was 10. She claims features like auto scrolling got her hooked, leading to anxiety, depression and body image issues. Lori Shotts' 18-year-old daughter, Anna Lee, took her own life after her mother says she became addicted to social media, Instagram in particular, using beauty filters and becoming obsessed with the way she looked.

title: Macron in India: French President Macron Arrives in Mumbai, India | WION
transcription: French President Emmanuel Macron and First Lady Brigitte Macron have arrived in Mumbai. They are on an official three-day visit to India, which will conclude on February 19th. The couple will be received, was received at the airport by Maharashtra Governor and Chief Minister. The visit marks Macron's fourth visit to the country at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mumbai's Badra Worli Sea Link lit up to welcome the French President. It was lit with pictures of the two leaders. Macron's first visit was in 2018, followed by his attendance at the 2023 G20 Summit and his 2024 state visit as the chief guest for India's 75th Republic Day. PM Modi will travel to Mumbai today where he will meet Macron. The two leaders will hold bilateral engagements at Lok Bhavan. During these engagements, they will review the progress made in the India-France strategic partnership. Their discussions will focus on cementing the strategic partnership and further diversifying it into new and emerging areas. They will also exchange views on issues of regional and global importance. Later in the day, the two leaders will inaugurate the India-France Year of Innovation 2026 and address a gathering of business leaders, startups, researchers, and other innovators from both the countries. Following their Mumbai engagements, the next day, the delegation will travel to New Delhi to attend the India AI Impact Summit 2026 that is being held at Bharat Mandapam. This event marks the first global AI summit hosted in the Global South.

title: 2026 Tesla Cybertruck Complete Review - Features, Performance, Design & Tech Explained in Detai
transcription: So you've seen it on the road. That angular stainless steel wedge that looks like it rolled straight out of a science fiction movie. The 2026 Tesla Cybertruck isn't just another electric pickup truck. It's a statement on wheels that challenges everything we thought we knew about what a truck should be. Whether you love it or hate it, you can't ignore it, and that's exactly the point. Starting at around $80,000 for the standard O-wheel drive model and topping out near 117,000 for the Cyberbeast True. The Cybertruck positions itself as a premium electric pickup. The exterior is built from what Tesla calls hard freaking stainless, a proprietary cold rolled stainless steel alloy that's roughly 1.8 mm thick on the doors and 1.4 mm on the body panels, Capital 1. This isn't just for looks. The material resists dings and dents far better than traditional sheet metal, Capital 1. Though you'll need to baby it a bit since it can still scratch and pick up surface contamination. The Cybertruck features steer-by-wire technology and four-wheel steering, Tech Times, making this massive truck surprisingly maneuverable in tight spaces. Under the angular body, you'll find an 816-volt battery pack with a capacity of 123 kilowatt hours, Wikipedia. Range varies from 318 to 340 miles, depending on configuration, Cars. And when you need to charge, the system can add significant range in just 15 minutes at high-powered stations. Performance is where this truck gets genuinely wild. The all-wheel drive version pumps out 600 horsepower and sprints to 60 miles per hour in just 4.1 seconds. While the top tier Cyberbeast cranks out 845 horsepower and hits 60 in a blistering 2.6 seconds, Kelly Blue Book. Yes, you read that correctly. This is a full-size pickup truck that accelerates faster than most sports cars. Both versions can tow up to 11,000 pounds and handle payloads exceeding 2,200 pounds, True car. So it's not all show and no go. Inside, minimalism reigns supreme with an 18.5 inch central touchscreen, controlling virtually everything. Torque you from climate to suspension height. Rear passengers get their own 9.4 inch screen, and the cabin features a 15 speaker audio system, Cars. The interior embraces utility over traditional luxury with durable materials designed to handle real work and play. title: Behind the NVIDIA CES 2026 Keynote: Creating a 12K, 20-Robot On-Stage Scene
transcription: When we were creating imagery for the Nvidia CES keynote, one of our goals was to create a high-fidelity group shot of 20 specific robots. We realized early on that a primary technical challenge was pixel density. Current generative models are limited to 4K or 5K resolution. So each robot occupied too small an area for fine detail. For this major keynote, we also needed a flexible workflow that allowed for rapid iterations without rebuilding the entire scene. Here's how we solved it. We began by generating low fidelity 3D models from reference images. While these were rough placeholders, they provided exactly what we needed to establish the initial layout for every robot in the set. Then, we brought these models into 3D software to assemble the scene. This gave us the flexibility to explore different compositions with total accuracy and control before committing to high resolution assets. Once the layout was locked, we exported the scene. While the final lighting and fine robot details weren't perfect, the scene gave us the precise coordinates we needed. We took the exact angle of every robot and went back to our reference images to generate fully detailed 4K individual assets that fit the composition perfectly. In Photoshop, we reconstructed the layout using these high-quality robot images. The result was a clean, high fidelity composition where every element was sharp and correctly positioned. Next, we used Weavy to build a custom AI agent that let us rapidly iterate on various lighting themes. Once the creative direction was settled, we generated the full 4K scene with the final look and lighting, then upscaled it to 12K. Given the complexity of generating 20 characters in a single pass, we took a targeted approach to the robot details, regenerating our high-detail robot assets specifically to match the new lighting environment and integrate seamlessly into the final composition. We brought these light-matched high detail robots back into Photoshop and merged them into the composition to restore all the lost texture and sharpness. After final touch ups to clean the scene, we produced a massive 12K high detail environment built specifically for the giant keynote screen. This workflow allowed us to handle change requests rapidly, maintain full control over the composition, look, and detail of every individual component, and bring the scene to life just as we had envisioned.

questions.answer: The primary technical challenge was pixel density. Current generative models were limited to 4K or 5K resolution, which meant each of the 20 robots occupied too small an area to render fine details.

questions.answer: Weavvy was used as a custom AI agent that allowed the team to rapidly iterate on various lighting themes for the scene after the composition was established.

questions.answer: The final resolution was a massive 12K. It was created specifically for the giant keynote screen at the NVIDIA CES event.

title: Why Bad Bunny wore “64” on his Super Bowl 2026 halftime jersey — and what it represents
transcription: From album of the year to the biggest stage in sports, Bad Bunny just turned the Super Bowl halftime show into a full-on celebration of Puerto Rico. But one detail from his outfit has fans talking, the number 64 stitched onto his jersey. So what does it mean? The show featured surprise appearances from Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin and transformed the field into a vibrant tribute to Puerto Rican culture. Style-wise, the details were just as intentional. He wore an Audemars Piguet watch, a Marquis diamond stud earring by Marvin Douglas, designed to echo the shape of a football, and a custom white football jersey by Zara. The jersey featured the name Ocasio, a nod to his real name Benito Antonio Martinez Ocasio. And now there's more clarity around the number 64 stitched across his chest. According to Complex, Bad Bunny was paying tribute to his late uncle, who previously played football and wore the same number. Before that detail emerged, fans had floated several theories. Some believed the number referenced his mother's birth year. Others connected it to the initial, widely criticized death toll reported after Hurricane Maria devastated Puerto Rico in 2017. There were even historical interpretations, including a nod to the 64th United States Congress, which passed the Jones-Shafroth Act granting U.S. citizenship to Puerto Ricans in 1917. Some pointed to 2023 when Bad Bunny's Un Verano Sin Ti became the first Spanish language album ever nominated for Album of the Year at the 64th Grammy Awards. At the 2026 Grammys, he made history again, winning Album of the Year for De Mi Tirar Mas Fotos, the first Spanish-language album to ever take home the top prize. That same night, he also turned heads on the red carpet in Schiaparelli's first-ever menswear design, and used his acceptance speech to protest ICE, declaring, we are humans and we are Americans. Those moments echoed into the halftime show, where he appeared to symbolically present his Grammy to a child watching his speech on a small TV, a powerful visual about legacy and representation. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell later praised the artist, saying Bad Bunny understood the weight of the platform and its power to unite people. Ahead of the game, an emotional Bad Bunny said the performance was about joy, culture, and heart, and dedicated it to those who came before him. With this latest confirmation, the meaning appears deeply personal, a family tribute layered into a performance already packed with cultural pride, history, and legacy.

transcription: Welcome back to the Pink City. Our journey through Jaipur continues, moving beyond the main squares into the city's hidden heart. Hidden near a mayor, the Panna Meena ka Kund is a geometric marvel. Its symmetrical stairs weave a pattern of shadows and light. Watching over the city is Jaigarh Fort, home to the massive Jaivana cannon, a silent guardian of the royals. If you like this content, please help us by hitting the subscribe button and notification bell so you can be notified when we upload additional content. At the foothills, silence reigns at Gatore ki Chhatriyan. These royal cenotaphs are carved with the delicacy of lace. In stark contrast to the Pink City, the Birla Mandir rises in pristine white marble, glowing softly under the sun. Escape the heat in the tiered gardens of Sisodia Rani Ka Bagh, a symbol of royal love and leisure. No walk is complete without a taste of Jaipur's famous lassi, served thick and creamy in earthen clay cups. And for the sweet tooth, there is ghevar, a honeycomb delicacy soaked in syrup, essential to any Rajasthani feast. In the workshops of Sanganer and Bagru, rhythmic thuds tell the story of handblock printing, an art form kept alive for centuries. The streets are a timeline of eras. Camel carts share the road with modern cars in a uniquely Indian harmony. At the Govind Dev Ji temple, the city's spiritual pulse beats strongest, drawing thousands in devotion. The Sargasuli tower pierces the skyline, offering a bird's eye view of the labyrinthine bazaars below. On street corners, vibrant Kathputli puppets tell ancient tales of kings and heroes. Moving to the modern city, Jawahar Circle claims to be the largest circular park in Asia. In the Maniharan Karasta, the heat of the furnace shapes the famous lac bangles, adorning the wrists of women. Even cinema is a royal affair here. The Rajmandir is not just a theater, it's a palace for Bollywood dreams. As twilight deepens, statue circle becomes a gathering point for families and friends. The city honors its brave at the Amar Jawan Jyoti, glowing solemnly in the darkness. Modern Jaipur shines just as brightly, blending its heritage with the stride of progress. From its royal past to its vibrant present, Jaipur is a city that never stops enchanting. This concludes our tour. title: How To Filter By Amenities In Airbnb App (Working 2026)
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to filter Airbnb listings by amenities on your iPhone. If you're looking for a place that absolutely has Wi-Fi, a kitchen or a pool, using the built-in filters will save you time and make your search a lot more precise. I'll walk you through the exact taps and what to expect on screen so you can get the most relevant results right away. Start by opening the Airbnb app on your iPhone. You should land on the home tab with the search bar near the top. Next, tap start your search at the top of the screen. This opens the search experience and brings up the keyboard so you can tell Airbnb what you're looking for. Type your destination to get the ball rolling. You can also add dates and the number of guests if you want your results to reflect real availability and pricing, but the key is to run the search so the results list is showing. Once results are on the screen, you'll see options running along the top. Find and tap filters at the top beside the results screen. This opens a full panel of options that help you narrow things down. There are different sections here, and the one we need is amenities. Scroll down until you reach the amenities section. Don't worry if you don't see the exact item right away. Just keep scrolling. Airbnb organizes amenities into clear labeled groups. Now tap the amenities you want. For example, choose Wi-Fi if you need a reliable internet connection, kitchen if you plan to cook or pool if a swim is non-negotiable. You can select multiple amenities at once and each one you tap will highlight to confirm it's selected. A quick tip, the more amenities you require, the fewer places you'll see. So focus on what's essential to your trip. When you're done selecting, apply your choices by tapping show places or save at the bottom right. This action updates your search and returns you to the results list with the filters active. You should notice the number of listings adjust right away. As you scroll through, look for amenity icons and details in each listing to confirm they match what you selected. If you want to refine things further, you can always go back to filters and adjust your amenities. Your previous selections will still be there. And if results feel too limited, remove a non-essential amenity to broaden the options. That's it. You've used Airbnb's amenities filter to quickly find stays that fit your needs all from your iPhone. Happy searching and enjoy your trip planning.

title: Never Before Filmed Moments Emperor Penguin Chicks’ Most Daring Moment | Arctic Nature Documentary
transcription: In the vast, frozen heart of Antarctica, a new generation of emperor penguins faces its first great test. Their parents have gone to sea, leaving hundreds of fluffy chicks huddled together for warmth in a massive crèche. For weeks they have waited, but now, an ancient instinct stirs within them. Hunger gnaws, and the call of the ocean becomes too strong to ignore. Led by an unseen force, this army of youngsters begins a determined march across the ice. It's a journey no one taught them, a path etched into their very being. Their destination is the sea, the source of all life and food. But the route this year is different. It leads them not to a gentle, sloping shore, but to the edge of a sheer 50-foot ice cliff. A colossal, frozen wall stands between them and their future. They peer over the edge, a chattering, nervous crowd, contemplating an impossible drop. The wind whips around them, and the icy water churns far below. Hesitation hangs in the air. For a young penguin, this is a terrifying, unprecedented challenge. Then, a moment of pure courage. A single chick steps forward, shuffles to the very brink, and without a second thought, takes a leap of faith. It plummets through the air, a tiny feathered projectile, and vanishes into the frigid depths with a splash. A beat of silence, and then it resurfaces, alive. This one act of bravery shatters the fear. Inspired, another follows, and then another. Suddenly, it's a cascade of courage. A torrent of chicks pours over the cliff edge, a spectacular, never-before-filmed event. Hundreds of them are making the plunge, a mass jump into the unknown. Down in the water, a new lesson begins. They are clumsy at first, wings flapping awkwardly as they learn to navigate this alien liquid world. V, they discover how to propel themselves, how to dive, and how to become the sleek, underwater flyers they were born to be. This incredible leap marks the start of their new life in the ocean. A powerful testament to the resilience and raw instinct of nature's youngest survivors. It's a harsh and beautiful beginning, and their great adventure has only just begun. Thanks for watching. And if you enjoyed this journey, don't forget to like and subscribe for more incredible stories from the wild.

transcription: Bastille Day started several years ago when the city of Paris, Texas that is, decided to promote itself to the outside world. They wanted to show off their schools, their industry, their lifestyles. And why not? Paris has a rich history, offering the glory of the old South and the excitement of the 20th century. This year, the city's newest addition to the celebration was a miniature version of the Eiffel Tower. And wishes to thank Mr. Herb Gifford for making it possible. The man they're talking about is 73-year-old Herb Gifford of Medford, Oregon. a kindly retired lumberman who finds his fun nowadays in carpentry, building stilts and wooden puzzles for the young people of Medford. Several years ago, Herb was inspired to build the Eiffel Tower. My youngest boy was in the band at the college and they took a tour of Europe. And when he was over there, he sent my wife and I a postcard of the Eiffel Tower. So I told my wife that we'll never get to Paris. We're going to bring a little Paris to Medford, so I'm going to build an Eiffel Tower in our backyard. Then I decided it'd be great on a city park, but the city park didn't want it. And I have an older boy that lives in Texas, and he says, 'There's a Paris in Texas. They could use your Eiffel Tower. The original Eiffel Tower was 984 ft tall, made of iron and built in three months. Herb's creation, smaller by 940 ft, and constructed of pine and Douglas fur, took almost two years to complete. title: Ellie Goulding BREAKS SILENCE on Panic Attacks After Sudden Rise to Fame
transcription: Ellie Goulding has pulled back the curtain on the not so glamorous side of fame, admitting her rapid rise to stardom came with a heavy emotional price. The chart-topping singer revealed she suffered panic attacks so severe she struggled to leave the house, despite being at the peak of her success. While fans saw sold-out shows, red carpets, and hit singles, Ellie says behind closed doors she was overwhelmed, anxious, and battling intense fear triggered by the sudden spotlight. According to Ellie, the shift from a normal, low-key life to global recognition happened almost overnight, and her mental health simply couldn't keep up. She described feeling constantly watched, judged, and under pressure to perform, which only fueled her anxiety. The panic attacks became so intense that everyday tasks felt impossible, highlighting the harsh reality that fame doesn't always equal happiness. It's a reminder that success can sometimes come faster than the ability to emotionally process it. Thankfully, Ellie says she's now in a much healthier place. Through therapy, self-reflection, and learning her limits, she's found ways to manage her anxiety and regain control of her life. By opening up, she hopes to break the illusion of perfect pop star life and encourage more honest conversations around mental health in the industry. But it leaves fans wondering, is the price of fame becoming too high for young stars to pay? Thanks for watching.

title: Justin Bieber to Perform at Grammy Awards
transcription: Justin Bieber to perform at Grammy Awards. Bieber, nominated for Album of the Year for Swag, is performing on the show for the first time since 2022. Justin Bieber will perform at the Grammy Awards this weekend, the Recording Academy confirmed on Sunday, marking Bieber's first time performing on music's biggest night since the 64th Grammys in 2022. Bieber is up for four Grammys this year, including for album of the year for Swag, his first record since 2021's Justice. He's also up for best pop vocal performance, best pop vocal album, and best R&B performance. Public performances from Bieber have been rare in the past few years during the singer's hiatus between Justice and Swag. He's set to headline Coachella this April in what's shaping up to be one of the biggest festivals Coachella has organized in years, with tickets quickly selling out when they were listed last fall. The academy said there'd be more performances announced in the coming days. The Grammy Awards are set to air live this Sunday on CBS and Paramount Plus starting at 5:00 p.m. This will be the last year the ceremony airs on CBS, ending a decades-long partnership as the show will move to Disney next year. This is also Trevor Noah's last time hosting the show, ending a six-year streak in which the comedian has served as MC.
