title: The "Lonely Penguin" Meme Explained: Why is 2026 So Existential? #penguin
transcription:
If you've scrolled through your feed recently, you have likely seen him. A single, determined penguin waddling away from his colony, heading straight toward the mountains of Antarctica. There is no music, just the sound of the wind and a narrator asking one simple, haunting question. But why?
Welcome back to Trends Deep Dive. Today, we are exploring the penguin mentality, why a clip from a 2007 documentary is the biggest motivational meme of 2026, and what it says about our obsession with the hero's journey. The footage comes from the legendary filmmaker Werner Herzog in his documentary Encounters at the End of the World. In the scene, Herzog observes a penguin who has lost its sense of direction. Instead of heading to the sea with the rest of the colony, it turns around and heads toward the interior of the continent, 70 km of frozen wasteland and certain death. Herzog famously asks, but why? And in 2026, that question has become a digital anthem for anyone who feels like they don't fit in. On TikTok and Instagram, this clip has been rebranded as the ultimate vibe check for independence. It represents the penguin mentality, the feeling of wanting to walk away from your responsibilities, from the herd and from the expectations of society. While the actual penguin in the film is considered disoriented by scientists, the internet has transformed him into a philosopher. He is the lone wolf of the Antarctic. He is the symbol of someone who would rather walk toward the mountains and face the unknown than stay in a safe, boring colony. In 2026, this meme is being used to celebrate the Faustian spirit. It is the urge to seek something greater than yourself, even if the path is difficult or lonely. We see it paired with captions about quitting a soul-crushing job, moving to a new city, or simply choosing to be alone to find yourself. It is a mix of irony and deep existential sincerity. We laugh at the waddling bird, but we secretly see ourselves in him. So, are you heading for the ocean with the colony? Or are you looking at the mountains? Let us know in the comments. Is the penguin mentality inspiring or just a sign that we are all a little lost in 2026? If you want to dive deeper into the memes that define our era, make sure to subscribe to Trendss Deep Dive. I will see you in the next one.

title: ByteDance Finalises TikTok Deal To Avoid US Ban; Donald Trump Lauds New Joint Venture | N18G
transcription: TikTok's Chinese parent company ByteDance says it has finalized a move to avoid a ban in the US. The deal will create a new majority American-owned joint venture aimed at protecting US user data. It's a major step after years of scrutiny by President Donald Trump, who in 2020 unsuccessfully tried to ban the app over national security concerns. In a post on Thursday, Trump said he is, quote, so happy to have helped in saving TikTok. He also lauded the deal, thanking Chinese President Xi Jinping for, quote, working with us and ultimately approving the deal. The TikTok USDS joint venture will be responsible for securing US data and apps and TikTok's recommendation algorithm. Under the agreement, American and global investors will own 80.1% of the venture, while ByteDance keeps the rest. Tech giant Oracle, private equity group Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi-based MGX will serve as managing investors, each holding 15%. A White House official says both the US and Chinese governments have approved the deal. The venture will retain and secure TikTok's algorithm using only US data, which will be secured on Oracle's cloud system. Reuters sources said last year that ByteDance would still own TikTok's US operations, but that control of data, content, and algorithms would shift to the new venture.

questions.answer: The main purpose of the new joint venture is to protect US user data and avoid a ban of the TikTok app in the United States.

title: How does protest music spread?
transcription: Okay, so that question, um, you know, asks about a very sort of new era of music making, right? We're talking about Spotify, we're talking about social media and new media technologies. And, uh, that really applies to about the last 20 years of music making in the world, right? A little bit more than 20 years perhaps, um, in the West. We can definitely say that social media and new me media changed the way in which music could be made and spread, and this certainly affected the volumes of music that were made by underground musicians both in Iran and the rest of the Middle East, in getting their their music out there. But that's not to say that, uh, you know, this couldn't be done prior to new media. So, prior to new media, small media still existed. What we mean by small media is, you know, not the big media such as state television, satellite television, and so on, but cassette tapes. Cassette tapes were small media. These were tapes that anybody could record and spread quite easily. In fact, the Iranian Revolution of 1979 uh owes a great debt to to this very small medium of the cassette tape whereby Khomeini's sermons were copied, you know, on hundreds of cassette tapes from his seat in France, Nofle-le-Chateau in France, and brought into uh, you know, sort of recorded over the telephone onto tapes in Iran and then multiplied there and spread among the population. So, prior to new media, we had that. And uh musicians would record and spread at great risk to their own personal safety and security in most of these contexts. And certainly with new media, that risk still exists, but musicians have taken great um advantage of the affordances of new media and, you know, things like Spotify to spread their music. I think it's worth saying that another thing that's that new media have facilitated is for the diaspora. Because a lot of these uh, you know, Middle Eastern um countries have huge diasporas because of the tumultuous decades which all of them have at this point experienced over the last four decades or more. There are huge diasporas of all of these countries around the world in Europe, in the US and further east in Asia. And so new media has also allowed them to partake in music making for dissent and protest in their home countries. They've been able to contribute to protest music within these countries.

title: When Beer Turned Into a Tsunami | The London Beer Flood (1814)
transcription: It was October 17th, 1814, in the St. Giles district of London, a working class area known for narrow streets and dense buildings. The Meux and Company Brewery, a giant operation storing hundreds of thousands of gallons of beer in massive wooden vats. One vat held around 135,000 gallons of porter, strong, dark beer that was a staple of Londoners' diets at the time. Early that morning, disaster struck. One of the enormous wooden vats burst suddenly. The immense pressure caused by fermentation had built up over time. Think of it as a natural soda bottle explosion, but on a massive scale. When the vat broke, it released 135,000 gallons of beer in seconds. But that wasn't all. Another vat, already weakened, collapsed under the force. Soon, a chain reaction sent thousands of gallons gushing through the streets. Wooden beams, barrels, and brewing equipment were swept away in a frothy flood. Eyewitnesses described it as a liquid wall of beer, brown and foaming, smashing fences, walls, and buildings. The flood reportedly reached two-story heights in some places, carving a path of destruction through homes and shops. The flood killed at least eight people, including workers and residents. Most of them were trapped under debris or swept away by the torrent of beer. The brewery faced a huge financial loss, around 23,000 pounds, which was an enormous sum at the time. Surprisingly, insurance didn't cover everything because this type of disaster was considered so unusual. The London beer flood quickly became legendary, inspiring songs, stories, and even jokes about beer as a destructive force. It also highlighted the dangers of industrial scale brewing in cramped urban areas. Today, the event is remembered as a bizarre cautionary tale. Too much beer in the wrong place can be deadly. So next time you lift a pint, remember, in 1814, Londoners didn't just drown in work, poverty or crime, they were almost drowned in beer itself. A historical tsunami fueled entirely by alcohol.

title: Tesla Lithium Refinery
transcription: This refinery is the first spodumene to lithium hydroxide refinery in North America. We're deploying a new technology platform that is inherently uh much more environmentally friendly and cleaner. It's a simpler process, it's a less expensive process. I'm Jason Bevan, I'm the site manager for Tesla's Gulf Coast lithium refinery just outside of Corpus Christie, Texas. Spodumene is a lithium-containing ore. It's a hard rock material that is rich in lithium. We sustainably source spodumene and bring it to site, where we then run it through a series of conveyance systems, take it through a kiln and cooler. From there, we take it through an alkaline leech and additional purification steps, take it into crystallization and produce battery-grade lithium hydroxide. Our process is more sustainable than traditional methods and eliminates hazardous byproducts and instead produces a co-product named analcime used in concrete mixes. From breaking ground in 2023 to running rock through the kiln in 2024 to start a full integrated plant startup now in 2025, we've achieved the fastest time to market for this first of its kind technology. By removing many of the traditional stage gate hurdles seen in large projects, we were able to complete feasibility, design, and construction in parallel, significantly accelerating our construction timeline. This refinery really enables us to have access to the critical minerals for energy storage, for battery manufacturing, and ultimately for EV growth. and it enables us to accelerate Tesla's mission by regionalizing supply chains for battery minerals and materials, by providing jobs, by cutting emissions from the transportation network that's required for those supply chains. It really allows us to usher in energy independence for North America.

title: At least 32 killed after crane collapses on train in Thailand - 14/Jan/2026
transcription:
At least 22 people have died and more than 80 more have been injured after a crane fell on top of a moving train carriage in Thailand. It happened near the city of Nakhon Ratchasima. It's around 160 miles northeast of Bangkok. The crane was working on a new rail construction project when it fell and struck a moving train causing it to derail briefly. The state rail authority there has said 195 people were on board. 

At least 32 people have been killed after a construction crane collapsed onto a train in Thailand. Around 80 others have been injured. The crash happened around 150 miles northeast of the capital Bangkok. Our Southeast Asia correspondent Jonathan Head joins us now from the scene. So, Jonathan, what more can you tell us about what happened?

I'm actually standing on the railway line where this happened and behind me they've moved away now using heavy cranes the crushed carriages. If I get the camera operator to tilt up a bit, you can see this is a brand new high-speed line that they're building on top of this existing railway line. And that huge crane you can see above me, that is now tilted at a really dangerous angle. Big parts of it came crashing down, crushing at least three of the carriages, setting one of them on fire. It really was a dreadful scene. They're trying to clear it up now. There are dozens of people still being treated in hospital, and the government has announced what it says will be a very fast investigation into what went wrong. But this is a highly prestigious project. This new railway line is meant to link Bangkok with China. It's part of China's Belt and Road initiative. So it's a very prestigious project and to have such a major disaster happen on it is a real blow to what for Thailand was meant to showcase its modernizing infrastructure. There have, I have to say, been other accidents like this before in Thailand. I think there'll be a lot of skepticism about what kind of action is going to follow this one.

transcription: Number six, Pulse nightclub, Kochani, North Macedonia. On March 16th, 2025, the Pulse nightclub in Kochani, North Macedonia became the site of one of the deadliest nightclub fires in recent European history. 63 people died and 193 were injured when fire swept through the venue. The fire started exactly as so many others had. Sparks from indoor fireworks hit the ceiling and set it alight. Collective nightclub, Bucharest, Romania. On October 30th, 2015, the Collective nightclub in Bucharest, Romania was hosting a free concert by the metalcore band Goodbye to Gravity, celebrating the release of their new album, Mantras of War. The band had announced in advance that they would be including customized lighting, pyrotechnic effects and scenic elements to give life to the science fiction artwork of the album. The venue was packed, a crowd of young people gathered to enjoy the music and celebrate with the band. But as the pyrotechnics were set off, consisting of sparkler firework candles, disaster struck. The fireworks ignited the club's flammable polyurethane acoustic foam that lined the walls and ceiling. The fire spread with terrifying speed. Most of the victims were poisoned by toxins released from the burning foam. Number four, Santika Club, Bangkok, Thailand. On January 1st, 2009, New Year's celebrations at the Santika Club in Bangkok, Thailand turned into a nightmare. Approximately 1,000 guests and employees were inside the club as midnight approached. Ironically, a band named Burn was performing as revelers counted down to the new year. But at 12:35 a.m., a fire broke out. No official cause has ever been announced by investigators, but suggested causes include outdoor fireworks that set the roof on fire, sparklers lit inside the nightclub, or an electrical explosion. One witness stated there were no pyrotechnics in the club, while another reported seeing flames on the roof after going outside to watch the midnight fireworks display.

title: NBA SUSPENDS Dennis Schröder 3 Games For Luka Dončić Confrontation। USA SportsLine

The league announced that Schroder sought out an opposing player, reportedly Dallas star Luka Dončić, in an arena hallway approximately 40 minutes after the Kings' loss to the Lakers on December 28th and initiated a confrontation, attempting to strike him. Schroder, a veteran of 13 NBA seasons, has been a key contributor, averaging 13 points and nearly six assists per game this year. He will miss the team's next three games against Houston, the Clippers, and New York. This isn't Schroder's first brush with controversy this season, as he was previously suspended one game for throwing his mouth guard at an official. The latest incident, involving a calculated post-game confrontation with another player, has drawn a sterner penalty from the league office. For a Kings franchise mired in a difficult year, losing a veteran leader for three games adds another layer of challenges as they navigate the rest of the season.

title: Los Angeles wildfires' anniversary puts focus on community resilience, recovery and remembrance
transcription: This week marks one year since the Eton and Palisades fires tore through neighborhoods across LA. The historic fires destroyed more than 16,000 buildings and claimed at least 30 lives and for many families, recovery is still far from complete. From above the scars of the Palisades and Eton fires are still unmistakable, reshaping entire neighborhoods in Altadena and Pacific Palisades. More than 16,000 buildings were destroyed and a year later, rebuilding remains slow and uneven. Recovery doesn't happen on an anniversary timeline. For many families, the road back has been slow, uncertain, and deeply frustrating. The mayor's office says more than 400 rebuilding projects are now underway in Pacific Palisades, but many residents are still displaced facing insurance delays and financial strain. A lawsuit against Southern California Edison over its alleged role in starting the fire is still under investigation.

Citizens whispered of the Carbonari, an Italian revolutionary group advocating for liberty and national unity. Their influence had seeped across the borders, igniting hopes among the French populace. As discontent bloomed, tensions escalated. On the morning of July 28th, crowds filled the streets, demanding the abdication of King Charles I 10th. They chanted revolutionary songs inspired by the whispers of the Carbonari. Meanwhile, clandestine meetings were held in darkened cafes where members plotted strategies and informed the masses. On that fateful day, barricades sprang up across the capital. By evening, the government was in chaos and the monarchy crumbled. The uprising proclaimed the July monarchy, forever intertwining the fates of Paris and the Carbonari. Thus the whispers transformed into a cry for freedom, echoing through the annals of history.

title: Mayor reflects 1 year after Palisades Fire, says people are profiting off of victims' grief
transcription: LA Mayor Karen Bass has faced criticism and anger from the community over her handling of the Palisades fire over the past year. Eyewitness News political reporter Josh Haskell walked through the Palisades with the mayor today to discuss the resentment that remains one year later. Palisades is always top of mind, and I'm not going to rest until Palisades looks like it did before January 7. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass was out of the country in Africa one year ago when the Palisades fire erupted. destroying nearly 7,000 structures. It was a rocky start to her response to the greatest disaster in the city's history, and there have been more challenges and scandals along the way. But at the one-year mark, Bass says she's inspired by the pace of rebuilding with 417 homes currently under construction. Even though there's lots of rebuilding going on, most people that are rebuilding are still not home. One year after the fires, are you surprised that so much of that anger is directed at you? A little, but again, I do understand the anger. If they need to focus them on me, you know, whatever, whatever takes them to heal and get through this. I don't take it personal. There's a rally being held tomorrow called they let us burn. Right. Is that how people should be commemorating this one-year anniversary? Well, well, I I don't think so. Again, I think that there are people that are profiting off of this. And that is what I find uh very despicable. Intentionally putting out misinformation, intentionally profiting from social media, book deals, etc. And I think that that's unfortunate. To me, I hope that it's about healing and moving forward and getting this community back. Every single Palisadian that wants to come back, that should be the focus. Bass has signed 13 executive directives aimed at expediting rebuilding, and residents we've spoken with say the permitting process with the city isn't what slowed them down, but rather insurance. Bass hopes those rebuilding recognize they're in a high fire severity zone. You have people who continue to tell me every single time I'm here, this should have never happened. Should this have ever happened? Of course it should have never happened, but I do think that something that we're all coming to grips with in our in our world, but certainly within our city, weather events that we would have never thought would have taken place in Los Angeles. But questions still remain about why the January 1st Lockman fire wasn't properly mopped up by the Los Angeles Fire Department, the role of California State Parks, and whether more people should be held accountable. Besides former LAFD Chief Kristen Crowley, who was fired by Bass last February. In Pacific Palisades, Josh Hascal, ABC 7 Eyewitness News.

title: Roborock Rover First Look - This is a GAME CHANGER!
transcription: Welcome to Vacuum Wars where we're covering the latest news coming out of CES 2026. And Roborock has just introduced a product that might finally solve one of the biggest limitations in the robot vacuum industry, and it's called the Roborock Seros Rover. And according to the company, it features the world's first robot vacuum with stair climbing legs. At IFA in Berlin last year, we saw brands like Dreamy, Mova and Eufy try to tackle the stair climbing issue with separate climbing modules that carried the robot itself up and down the stairs. But those modules are pretty big and they can't actually vacuum the stairs themselves. The robots just get carried up and down the stairs. The new Seros Rover uses a legs with wheels architecture where each wheel is paired with a leg like mechanism. These can deploy independently to keep the robot's body level on uneven surfaces, slopes, and yes, stairs. Roborock says that this design allows it to raise and lower each wheel independently, execute agile turns and perform movements intended to imitate human mobility. They're using AI algorithms paired with motion sensors and 3D spatial information to make this happen, which is much more in line with what's happening in humanoid robotics lately, and it's pretty exciting to see. This would presumably completely solve the threshold climbing issue, but the biggest win here for the robot vacuum industry is that the Seros Rover doesn't just climb, it cleans every step as it goes. Also, it seems to be significantly smaller than the other prototype stair climbers that we've seen so far. There's also demo footage showing the robot executing small jumps to clear laser obstacles and maintaining its balance while testers throw tennis balls at it. I'm not sure what the application of either of these would be for robot vacuums, but it all suggests that this technology isn't just about climbing, it's about physically reacting to a dynamic environment in a way that we just haven't seen before. Roborock does emphasize that the Seros Rover is currently in development and the launch date is unconfirmed. There are still major questions that we at Vacuum Wars still would like to be answered, and I hope to have some of those answers at least in our full coverage of CES 2026 in a video coming out this Friday. We will also be putting out short form videos on TikTok and YouTube Shorts all this week during CES. So, stay tuned for our big CES coverage video this Friday and be sure to subscribe to Vacuum Wars here on YouTube or TikTok to keep up with all the latest information about CES 2026.

title: Video Appears to Show Protesters Being Shot in Iran
transcription: A new video appears to show protesters in Iran being shot, and in an effort to ease Iran's economic crisis, Tehran has announced monthly cash payments to citizens. And today's Jason Perry has the details and the warning, this report contains footage that some viewers may find disturbing. In a video recently posted to social media, protesters in Iran were seen gathered outside the gate of what was said to be a police station. Then the sound of gunshots was heard as the protesters tried to run away. A few individuals appeared to have been shot as they were seen lying on the ground, and others later came to try to help them. The Kurdistan Human Rights Network said the incident happened over the weekend, and that Iranian forces killed three protesters and injured over 30 others in the incident in Western Iran. Residents in the country have been protesting for more than a week over the country's economic crisis. President Trump's maximum pressure campaign imposed crippling sanctions in an effort to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons. And Trump issued a warning recently saying that if Iran shoots peaceful protesters, then the US will, quote, come to their rescue. The US State Department posted this picture with a caption in Farsi, which translates to, don't play games with President Trump. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said this about his country's military readiness. Actions or statements by the Prime Minister of the Zionist regime, as well as by certain radical US officials, regarding Iran's internal affairs, are nothing but incitement to violence, terrorism, and killing in the language of international norms. And he added that Iran remains ready to defend its borders and, quote, its very existence. The Iranian government also announced efforts to ease the economic burden on residents. The government has passed a bill to pay all Iranian households. Let me emphasize that the household must be Iranian and residing inside Iran, $7 a month for each household member. title: Rome's Test: Tornado and Flood, the Harsh Reality of Italy
transcription: Severe weather struck Rome, Italy on the morning of January 4th. Flooded streets turned into raging streams with trees and branches falling directly onto the roads. City police responded to several emergency calls. Traffic on Via Lello Maddaleno was paralyzed by a flooded stream and a tornado in the Castelli Romani neighborhood. In Belpoggio, the access bridge had to be closed to prevent tragedy. More than 100 police and civil defense units were on the ground, directing traffic and closing roads. On Via Collatina, water and fallen branches completely blocked a section of the road. Bus routes were rerouted to avoid dangerous areas. Flooding also affected Via Carlo Calisse in the Cinità Lamaro district. Rome welcomed the new year battling a severe storm that served as a reminder of its destructive power.

The club thanked Amorim for his contribution and wished him well for the future. Amorim leaves after overseeing 63 games in charge, including taking United to the UEFA Europa League final in May, but also presiding over one of the club's poorest league finishes and inconsistent results this season. Former United midfielder Darren Fletcher has been appointed as interim head coach ahead of the team's next match against Burnley as the club begins its search for a new permanent manager. Fans are already debating who should take over next. Some say Erik ten Hag should return to Manchester United. title: How to Create a Slide Deck (Presentation) Automatically for FREE using Google NotebookLM
transcription: Hi everyone, welcome back. In this video, let's learn how to create a slide deck automatically using Google Notebook LM. No PowerPoint design, no manual slide creation, no copy pasting content. Just upload your material and notebook LM builds the presentation for you. Let's start from zero and do this step by step. First, let's open notebook LM in the browser. On the home page, let's click create new. A new notebook opens. At the top, let's rename it. For example, AI concepts slide deck. Now remember this rule, notebook LM creates slide decks only from the sources we add. So let's add our content. On the left side in the sources panel, let's click add sources. We can upload PDFs, add article links, paste copied text or even add YouTube videos. For this demo, let's add a PDF file that contains notes about AI. Click on upload files, select the PDF file and upload it. Once the source is added, notebook LM reads and understands the material. Now let's generate the slide deck. Move to the right side to the studio panel. Here, let's click slide deck. As soon as we click it, notebook LM analyzes our content. It identifies main topics, key points and supporting details. Then it automatically organizes everything into a structured presentation. While it's generating, we can see the customization options. Let's click the pencil icon. Here, we can choose the format. If we want detailed slides with full explanations, let's choose detailed deck. If we want clean slides to present live, let's choose presenter slides. Next, we can select the language. We can also choose the length, short, default or long. And we can add a prompt for example, create slides for beginners with simple examples. Now let's close this and wait for the deck to finish generating. Once it's ready, the slide deck appears inside the studio panel. Let's click to open it. Now we can scroll through the slides, start a full screen slideshow or review each slide one by one. If we want to share it, we can use the share option. And if we want to keep it, we can download it as a PDF file. That's it. We just converted raw content into a complete slide deck using Google Notebook LM. This is perfect for students, teachers and professionals who want fast presentations without extra effort.

title: B2 English Listening: How Smartphones Killed Traditional News! 📱
transcription:
Hello and welcome to Everyday English Kit. Listen carefully, try to understand the main ideas, and answer the questions at the end.
Stop the video and copy the questions or their numbers.
During the 2010 Arab Spring protests, ordinary citizens armed with smartphones outpaced traditional news crews.
Amira, a Cairo University student, live-streamed clashes from Tahrir Square when cameras were banned.
Although untrained, her raw footage, shaky but authentic, reached millions via Twitter.
Truth doesn't need studios, she posted. Citizen journalism exploded thereafter.
Platforms like YouTube democratized reporting. Bystanders captured events professionals missed.
Advantages abound, immediacy trumps delayed broadcasts, diverse perspectives challenge biases.
Yet pitfalls loom. Unverified videos spread misinformation, as seen in manipulated Ukraine war clips. 
Fact-checkers now verify sources rigorously. Amira evolved into a full-time journalist, blending citizen roots with ethical training.
Her documentary on refugee stories won awards, proving amateurs can professionalize.
Although critics decry lack of standards, data shows 60% of breaking news originates from eyewitnesses.
Governments regulate selectively, balancing free speech with accuracy. This shift empowers voices long silenced, though it demands media literacy from audiences.
Thank you for watching. Subscribe for more practice.

The bottom line is this, the expectation when we get the numbers from Tesla, which are likely going to happen a little before 9:00 a.m. Eastern time, if history holds in terms of when we see those numbers, it's going to be about 426,000. That is the fact set estimate that is out there. By the way, Tesla put out its own estimate based on its conversations with analysts, came in at 422,000. Regardless, compared to Q3, it's going to be down about 15% and for the year, the consensus is deliveries coming in at 1.64 million. To put that into some perspective compared to previous year, that will mark a second straight year with annual deliveries declining. They were down slightly last year at just over 1.78 million vehicles. Again, the expectation is that they're going to be down about 8.3% for all of 25 compared to 24. In terms of the regions, remember Tesla doesn't break their their deliveries out by the US, Europe and China. Deutsche Bank extrapolated the numbers based on the sales data that comes from each of those regions. and this is the expectation for the fourth quarter. Not a surprise that you see Europe and US down more than 30%. China, that continues to be a challenging market because of all the competition that has come in there. But when you look at shares of Tesla, why do they continue to move higher? Because deliveries are less and less an important statistic or metric, I should say, for investors to follow. What are they focused on? Robo taxi and autonomous develop vehicle development. Austin and San Francisco are the two robo taxi markets. Though Elon Musk said, look, we expect to be launched by the end of 25. That hasn't happened. title: About 40 killed in New Year’s Eve fire at Swiss Alps bar
transcription: Video from inside the New Year's celebration in the Swiss Alps shows the chaos as the deadly flames spread at a bar popular with young people and tourists. You can hear the screaming, people scrambling for the exit as the flames rip through the confined spaces of the bar Le Constellation. Swiss authorities say about 40 people were killed and more than 100 injured in the fire that began at 1:30 a.m. The cause of the blaze now under investigation, though Swiss officials say they've ruled out terrorism, calling the fire an accident that led to an explosion inside the bar. Just 90 minutes earlier, celebrations on the streets of the upscale ski resort Crans Montana. But what many thought were the sounds of New Year's Eve fireworks were in fact one of the worst tragedies Switzerland has ever experienced, according to the country's president. Aujourd'hui, la Suisse est triste. saying today Switzerland is mourning. This young woman says she was holding on to a friend as she escaped. She let go of his arm and now she says she can't reach him. Officials warn identifying the dead could take days. Many of those killed were from abroad. Witnesses describing the sheer panic as people tried desperately to escape. A lot of people were screaming, trying to escape, and I saw a lot of people on the floor and I think this people was dead. Officials say first responders were on the scene within minutes and the fire was quickly put out. Many so badly burned, they were taken to various hospitals across the country. The grueling work of identifying the dead and notifying their families is now underway. And Danielle joins me now from the scene in Switzerland. Danielle, it is just heartbreaking. There's a lot of speculation about the cause of the fire and if a sparkler might have been involved? Yeah, Kate, some of those who escaped talked about how champagne bottles had lit sparklers in them and that they were waved, some of them pretty high, hitting the ceiling, and then that's how the fire started. But authorities are saying it is too early to confirm an official cause. We thank you for watching and remember, stay updated on breaking news and top stories on the NBC News app or watch live on our YouTube channel.

title: Nvidia’s $5 billion Intel bet just became official
transcription: Nvidia's $5 billion Intel bet just became official. Intel confirmed it completed Nvidia's $5 billion share sale on December 26th after regulatory clearance, formalizing Nvidia's roughly 4% stake. What began as a September announcement now sits as settled cash and issued shares on Intel's balance sheet. Nvidia bought 214,776,632 Intel shares at $23.28 each in a private placement. The long-awaited cash infusion landed as a visible vote of confidence, ending months of future tense speculation and transforming a pending deal into finalized ownership. Nvidia's buy-in price was 36% below Intel's prior Friday close, underlining the leverage of a market heavyweight. Early trading showed Nvidia down about 1.7% while Intel stayed mostly flat, as the headline became a routine regulatory filing. The private placement granted Nvidia no special governance or information rights beyond standard shareholders. Federal Trade Commission early termination of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period on December 18th cleared the final regulatory hurdle, shifting the deal from pending to fully done. Jensen Huang described the partnership as historic, noting teams have co-developed architecture across CPUs, servers and PCs for over a year. He framed the investment as the next step in reinventing computing layers driven by accelerating artificial intelligence demand. Analysts likened the pairing to longtime rivals uniting. Earlier, the federal government engineered a roughly 10% Intel equity stake, signaling industrial policy backing. In President Donald Trump's AI posture, Intel emerged as a corporate vessel for made here ambition. Intel and Nvidia plan to co-develop data center and PC products, including custom X86 CPUs and hybrid system on chips. The deal omits any pledge to move Nvidia GPUs from TSMC. For Intel, the cash and association bolster credibility. For Nvidia, it eases entry into X86 ecosystems.

title: Intel Analog Engineer Technical Interview Question Walkthrough
transcription: Welcome back to Voltage Learning. Let's walk through this Intel analog engineer question because it touches on a very common bring-up issue that trips up even experienced designers. The question asks, during bring-up, an op-amp configured as a voltage follower shows an output that rails high even when the input is at mid-supply. Which condition most commonly causes this behavior? At first glance, this can feel confusing. After all, a voltage follower is supposed to simply mirror the input. But the key insight here is that negative feedback only works if the op-amp is operating within its valid input range. Even though the circuit uses feedback, the op-amp's input pins still must stay within the device's input common mode range. If the input voltage exceeds that range, often because the op-amp is not rail to rail on its inputs, the internal input stage can saturate. When that happens, the feedback loop effectively breaks down. The op-amp can no longer regulate properly, and the output often slams into one of the supply rails, frequently the positive rail during bring-up. Now, let's briefly rule out the other options. High open loop gain is normal and expected. It doesn't cause an output to rail by itself. Slew rate limits how fast the output can move, not where it settles in steady state. And a lighter output load actually makes it easier for the op-amp to drive the correct voltage, not harder. So the correct answer is, the input common mode exceeds the op-amp's valid range. This is exactly the kind of issue that shows up during early lab bring-up and silicon validation. Intel interviewers like this question because it tests whether you understand that data sheet limits still apply, even in seemingly simple configurations like voltage followers. If you want analog explanations grounded in real world debug scenarios, not just textbook theory, that's what Voltage Learning is built to deliver.

questions.answer: The most common cause is the input voltage exceeding the op-amp's valid input common-mode range, which causes the internal input stage to saturate and the feedback loop to break down.

title: Flat-Headed Cat Filmed In Thailand – The First Confirmed Sighting In Almost 30 Years
transcription: Flat-headed cats have been successfully detected and filmed in southern Thailand for the first time in almost 30 years. One of the world's rarest cats, it was last documented here back in 1995, leading some to believe it was possibly extinct. Conservationists, however, thought otherwise. We had heard reports for many years and were confident that the species was still present. Rettapan Padinarinsen, conservation program manager for Panthera Thailand, told IFL Science. What was needed was the right study design to confirm it. The largest ever survey of the species began in 2024, using camera traps from Thailand's Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, and Panthera Thailand, a global wildcat conservation organization. 13 detections were made in 2024, and a further 16 detections were made in 2025. Most exciting of all, the observations included a female flat-headed cat with her cub. Flat-headed cats are the smallest in Southeast Asia. They weigh half that of a typical domestic cat and have a distinctive flattened forehead and elongated skull. They are small, nocturnal and prefer to occupy dense terrain, making searching for them in the wild that much harder. Even catching them on camera traps can be difficult. But using lessons learned from studying fishing cats, Panthera were able to identify the best sites for camera placement, leading to the successful detection and photographic evidence of the flat-headed cat. It's estimated there are 2,500 flat-headed cats globally, and they're classed as endangered by the IUCN, but in Thailand, it was considered possibly extinct. A new Panthera-led IUCN assessment is now expected in 2026.

title: India Closes Visa Center in Chattogram After Anti-India Protests
transcription: Hello everyone. Today, we are discussing an important development in South Asia involving India and Bangladesh. Recently, anti-India protests were reported in different parts of Bangladesh. These demonstrations were organized by various groups who raised slogans against Indian policies and actions. During some of these protests, tensions increased and concerns were raised about the safety of Indian institutions and personnel in the country. Following these events, India decided to temporarily shut down its visa application center in Chattogram, one of the major port cities of Bangladesh. This decision was taken as a precautionary security measure. According to Indian officials, the visa center in Chattogram plays an important role, as thousands of Bangladeshi citizens apply for Indian visas every month. These visas are mainly used for medical treatment, education, business, tourism, and family visits. With the closure of the center, many applicants are now facing delays and uncertainty. Indian authorities stated that the decision was not meant to harm people-to-people relations but was necessary to ensure the safety of staff and visitors. They also clarified that the situation is being closely monitored and services may resume once conditions improve. On the other hand, officials in Bangladesh emphasized that they are committed to maintaining law and order and ensuring the security of foreign missions. Bangladesh and India share historically strong diplomatic, cultural, and economic ties, and both countries have worked closely on regional cooperation. Political analysts believe that such incidents highlight the sensitivity of public sentiment and the importance of diplomatic dialogue. While protests are a form of expression, any situation that threatens diplomatic operations can impact bilateral relations and ordinary citizens. Experts are also pointing out that visa services are a crucial link between the two nations. Any disruption affects students, patients, and families who depend on cross-border travel. In conclusion, the closure of the Indian visa center in Chattogram reflects growing concerns over security following recent protest. Both countries are expected to engage in dialogue to reduce tensions and restore normal services as soon as possible. Thank you for watching.

At its peak, nearly one-third of the city's customers were without power. City officials say the outage caused widespread traffic chaos, darkened street lights and Christmas decorations, and forced many restaurants and shops to shut their doors temporarily. Pacific Gas and Electric now says the city's power grid has been stabilized and no additional customer outages are expected. Power has been restored for about 95,000 customers in the city. However, the utility company has not confirmed when electricity will be fully restored to all affected areas. Public transport was also hit with uh mini buses and trains bypassing several stations due to the loss of electricity. title: ByteDance Signs Deal To Divest TikTok U.S. Assets | Asia One News
transcription: Tik Tok's parent company, ByteDance has signed binding agreements to sell most of the app's US assets and form a joint venture with American and international investors, a move aimed at avoiding a potential US ban on the popular video platform. Under the deal, ByteDance will reduce its ownership stake to below 20% while US-based investors including Oracle and Silver Lake will take significant holdings in the new joint venture. Abu Dhabi investment firm, MGX will also join the ownership group with the remaining shares held by existing bytedance investors. This agreement follows repeated delays ordered by US President Donald Trump on enforcing a law that would ban Tik Tok unless its US operations were sold. The transaction is expected to be completed by January 2026, allowing Tik Tok to continue operating in the US where it has more than 170 million users. US lawmakers first approved the ban in 2024 over national security concerns related to data handling and Chinese ownership. The current administration has since worked toward a negotiated sale rather than an outright shutdown of the platform.

title: Major quake in Tokyo area could kill up to 18,000: government estimate
transcription: The Japanese government released on December 19th new damage estimates for a major earthquake that could strike the Tokyo metropolitan area within 30 years with a 70% probability. The calculations assume a worst-case scenario involving a powerful shallow quake directly beneath Tokyo, registering the maximum seismic intensity of seven in the capital, and lower six or above over a wide area. According to the report, the number of fatalities could reach 18,000. Despite progress in earthquake resistance and fire prevention, the government fell short of its goal to halve estimated fatalities from its previous report 12 years ago. The latest figure is just 5,000 lower than the 2013 projection. The estimated economic damage has been set at 83 trillion yen. The report also points out that in Tokyo, in three surrounding prefectures where about 30% of Japan's population lives, there would be limits to administrative response as an extremely large number of people would be affected by the disaster. It recommends that people shelter at home when emergency assistance is not required and notes the need to view disasters as a personal matter and prepare in advance. カメラ撮りはよろしい

title: Get to know Control Center on Apple Vision Pro | Apple Support
transcription: Control Center gives you easy access to the controls you use the most on Apple Vision Pro. We'll show you how to access it and go over some of its unique features. Let's get started. You can access control center anytime. First, look at your hand with your palm facing you. Now turn your hand over so your palm is facing away from you. A status bar appears where you can check your battery level and time at a glance. Tap the status bar to open Control Center. On the left side, you'll find familiar controls like Wi-Fi, volume, and now playing. You can tap the appearance button next to your current environment to switch between light and dark appearance. In the upper right corner, you can tap to open notification center, or spotlight. On the right side, you can scroll to access essential controls. For example, Mac virtual display lets you bring your Mac wirelessly into Apple Vision Pro with an expandable ultrawide display. With guest user, you can let someone else try out your Apple Vision Pro while controlling what apps they can use. And travel mode helps you use Apple Vision Pro as a passenger on a plane, train, car, or bus. To exit control center, tap the close button in the upper left corner. You can change your control center options and settings. While looking at the left side of the settings window, scroll down to control center, and tap to select it. Here, you'll find more controls you can access in control center. Just tap the add button next to an item to add it. You can also change how you open control center if you prefer not to use the default gesture. On the left side of the settings window, look at accessibility, and tap to select it. Scroll down to the physical and motor section. Look at interaction and tap to select it. You can use look upwards for control center, which will give you a button to access control center. Tap to turn it on. and a slider appears that you can use to change the position of the button if you'd like. Now, let's close settings and open control center. You can now look up and tap the control center button, which looks like a small arrow at the top of your view. And that's how to access your most used controls anytime in Control Center on Apple Vision Pro.

title: Malvay Hand Massager Review – Is It Legit or a Scam? (Nuvra 3-in-1 Exposed)
transcription: Have you been seeing ads for the Malvi hand massager, also called the Novra 3 in one hand massager, claiming to relieve arthritis pain, carpal tunnel, and wrist strain in minutes? It promises compression, vibration, and heat therapy all in one device. But the real question is, is this product legit or just another overpriced online scam? In this video, I'll break down the biggest red flags, price discrepancies, and what you should know before buying. According to the official website, the Malvi or Novra hand massager claims to improve blood circulation, reduce stiffness and inflammation, relieve arthritis and carpal tunnel pain, help people who work long hours on computers. all using a single device with compression, vibration, and heat. Sounds impressive, but this is where we need to slow down and look closer. The first red flag is aggressive marketing. They push you to buy it for $119, making it feel like a premium medical grade device. But here's the problem. The same hand massager can be found at eBay for around $51.89. Same design, same features, less than half the price. This raises serious questions. Why is the official website charging more than double? Are you paying for quality or just marketing? Another major concern is the medical style claims. Relieving pain from arthritis, carpal tunnel, repetitive strain injuries. These are medical conditions and reliable treatments usually require professional guidance. Yet there are no clinical studies, no FDA approvals mentioned, and no credible medical endorsements. That's a big red flag. Any product claiming to fix multiple unrelated conditions should be questioned. Arthritis, nerve compression and muscle fatigue are very different problems. A single massager helping temporarily relax muscles is possible, but claiming long-term relief for all these conditions, that's unrealistic. When checking review platforms like Trustpilot, independent blogs and forums, there's a lack of verified customer reviews. Most reviews appear only on sales pages or sponsored articles. No detailed long-term user feedback. No verified buyer experiences. That's another warning sign. So is Malvi or Novra hand massager a scam? It's likely a real product but heavily overpriced and overmarketed. You're not paying for advanced technology, you're paying for aggressive advertising and exaggerated promises. If you've already used the Malvi or Novra hand massager, please leave a comment and share your experience to help others. Don't forget to like, subscribe and stay safe from online product scams.

title: ER visits for heart attacks surged in aftermath of January's LA County wildfires, study shows
transcription: New at 7:00 a.m. an important health study just released on the direct health effects of the LA fires. Some of it might some of it you might expect, but one huge finding is one researchers have never seen before. Circle of Health reporter Denise Dedor with what these new findings mean for all of us who live here. Oh my gosh. When we pulled up, we saw everything was like gone. Hours after evacuating, Claudine Ang and her children went back to see if their Altadena home was still standing. Fire had engulfed the garages and living quarters next to the main house. The family picked up garden hoses to fight the flames. Don't get too close, guys. It was an all-day battle. Just all the excitement of trying to put this fire out that kind of took over and we kind of didn't really think about our safety. Now, new research reveals you don't have to be that close for that long to experience immediate health effects. And we found that visits to the ER for respiratory illness increased by 24% after the wildfire started. And for 90 days after the fires, heart attacks rose 46%. But Dr. Susan Cheng, director of public health research at Cedar Sinai Smidt Heart Institute says, what scientists found next was peculiar and surprising. We've never seen anything like this before. Researchers tracked a 118% spike in patients with abnormal blood work, all needing emergency care. We can see that these are patients who came in with cough, but their chest x-ray was clear. They came in with dizziness, but there weren't signs of dehydration. They came in with chest pain, but they weren't having a heart attack. What did these abnormal lab results mean and what was the link to all these different unexplained symptoms? The January wildfire exposures seem to have led to some kind of a biochemical metabolic stress on the body that likely affected more than just one organ system. The medical center is located 10 miles from the Palisades fire and 20 miles from the Eton fire. But Dr. Cheng says the results she got at Cedar Sinai's ER could probably be replicated at any other ER here in LA County and maybe even as far south as Orange County. So we know that even beyond LA, many, many people were affected. Dr. Chen says most healthy people with this abnormal blood work appear to have recovered, but what are the potential long-term effects, if any? That needs more study. Meantime, especially on poor air quality days, her advice is to wear a mask and take advantage of air filtration. Those are two now tried and true proven strategies for mitigating and minimizing risk. With all these health concerns, it's really scary. Claudine says she wants to return home, but the findings give her mixed feelings. Happy, but worried at the same time. Especially for my kids. In Altadena, Denise De Dor, ABC 7, I Witness News.

title: OpenAI’s CEO Sam Altman Declares CODE RED
transcription: In early December 2025, Open AI CEO Sam Altman declared an internal code red, signaling a state of existential urgency for the company. This move, reminiscent of Google's own panic following the launch of chat GPT in 2022, was triggered by a sudden and significant loss of market momentum. For the first time, Open AI found its dominance directly threatened by the rapid ascent of Google's Gemini 3, which began outperforming chat GPT on critical benchmarks like humanity's last exam, and seeing 30% growth while chat GPT's user base plateau. The code red directive fundamentally shifted Open AI's operational priorities. To reclaim its lead, the company paused long-term experimental projects, including its push into advertising and the development of specialized AI agents for health and shopping to marshall resources toward the core product. Engineers were reallocated to focus on immediate improvements in reliability, speed, and professional utility. The first major outcome of this mobilization was the fast-tracked release of GPT 5.2 on December 11th, 2025. Marketed as a professional work partner, the new model introduced a tiered system, Instant, thinking and Pro, designed to match Gemini 3's reasoning capabilities. Internal data suggests GPT 5.2 reclaimed the top spot in coding and mathematical reasoning, achieving a perfect 100% on the AME 2025 math benchmark. Beyond the product race, the code red reflects a high stakes financial reality. With projected losses nearing $140 billion by 2029 and $1.4 trillion in infrastructure obligations, Open AI cannot afford to lose the smartest model title that fuels its subscription and enterprise revenue. By declaring a code red, Altman has signaled that the era of uncontested dominance is over, forcing Open AI to transition from a pioneering lab into a focused, defensive tech giant fighting for its survival in a saturated market.

questions.answer: The 'Code Red' was declared in response to the company losing market momentum to Google's Gemini 3, which had begun outperforming ChatGPT on critical benchmarks and was seeing significant user growth while ChatGPT's user base plateaued.

questions.answer: The company paused long-term experimental projects, such as its push into advertising and specialized AI agents, to reallocate resources and engineers toward making immediate improvements to its core product's reliability, speed, and professional utility.

questions.answer: The first product was the fast-tracked release of GPT-5.2 on December 11, 2025. It reportedly achieved a perfect 100% score on the AIME 2025 math benchmark.

title: TRAILER: The Malaria Challenge: a participant’s experience through a malaria ‘challenge’ study
transcription: Hello, my name is Angela Manasian. I lead on the malaria vaccine clinical trials program here in Oxford, in partnership with Professor Simon Draper, our lab and clinical team, and in collaboration with the Oxford Vaccine Group. The purpose of this documentary is to introduce you to the concept of a human malaria challenge study, where we deliberately infect healthy adults with malaria. This is something we've been doing in Oxford for more than 20 years. We do this to answer fundamental questions about the body's response to malaria. We also infect volunteers who have been given an experimental vaccine against malaria in order to give us an early indication of whether the vaccine is likely to work. And ultimately, these sorts of studies should help us to make better vaccines. You will hear from one of the doctors who runs our studies, Dr. Jennifer Van Heerden. You will also hear from one of our study volunteers who was deliberately infected with malaria, and she will give you a sense of her personal journey through our study. Going forward, we hope that our vaccines will build on the success of the current licensed vaccines, and the results from our human challenge studies will play an important part in this process. So don't just take my word for it. Listen and watch carefully and then make up your own mind as to whether human challenge studies are important for malaria.

title: Mexico City Legislature: Physical Clash Erupts Between Lawmakers
transcription: Tensions boiled over in a Mexico City Congress on Monday, leading to a physical confrontation between lawmakers from opposing political parties. This incident, which unfolded during a live television broadcast, involved members of the right-wing National Action Party, PAN, and the ruling leftist Morena party. The spark? A heated debate over proposed reforms to the city government's transparency oversight agency. According to reports, the PAN legislators, who are in the minority, approached the main podium to protest what they saw as a violation of legislative rules by Morena, which holds the majority. Video footage captured the chaotic scene, showing lawmakers shouting, shoving, and even pulling hair. The opposition party's goal was to physically block voting on the budget. But here's where it gets controversial. The PAN representatives accused the ruling party of using force to silence dissent, claiming they had taken the podium peacefully. On the other hand, Morena representatives rejected accusations of wrongdoing, arguing that the opposition had disrupted proceedings. And this is the part most people miss. The incident highlights a deeper issue, the increasingly polarized political climate. The PAN and Morena parties have very different views on how the city should be run, and this clash shows how those differences can sometimes lead to physical altercations. Following the incident, the PAN lawmakers exited the chamber, allowing Morena legislators and their allies to continue the debate. What do you think? Was the opposition justified in their actions, or did they overstep their boundaries? Did the ruling party overreact, or were they simply trying to maintain order? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: Cambodians in South Korea Protest Thai Military Strikes
transcription: More than 2,000 Cambodians in South Korea staged coordinated protests Saturday, denouncing what they call Thailand's brutal military aggression against Cambodia and demanding an immediate halt to hostilities. Demonstrations took place in Seoul and Gwangju, where protesters carried banners and chanted slogans, urging Thai forces to respect international law and abide by the Cambodia-Thailand ceasefire signed in Kuala Lumpur. In Seoul, more than 300 demonstrators marched near the Thai embassy and submitted a petition calling for an end to the violence. In Gwangju, over 2,000 Cambodians gathered in one of the largest overseas rallies since the latest escalation of border clashes. Organizers pressed Thailand to comply with humanitarian law and honor the peace agreement witnessed by US President Donald Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, ASEAN current chair. The rallies followed earliest demonstrations on December 13th across several South Korea cities, reflecting growing concern among overseas Cambodians communities over the conflict's humanitarian toll.

title: Alexander Isak Struggling at Liverpool Fans Question £125M Signing। USA SportsLine
transcription: With every passing week, Alexander Isak, Liverpool's record signing, is starting to feel less like a necessity and more like a luxury the Reds could do without. Last summer, Liverpool had made it clear, Isak was their dream forward, the striker to outshine Darwin Nunez, the player capable of carrying the club to Premier League glory for years to come. But the path to securing him was anything but straightforward. Negotiations with Newcastle United hit obstacles almost immediately. Liverpool's initial eye-watering offer was rebuffed, forcing the champions to turn their attention elsewhere. That elsewhere was Hugo Ekitike, a highly rated French forward who quickly became a Merseyside resident, seemingly closing the door on Isak. Yet the Swede's timely strike for Newcastle and a public declaration of broken promises kept the dream alive. Eventually, Liverpool won the long pursuit, paying 125 million pounds for a player with an incredible record of 44 goals across the previous two Premier League seasons. Expectations soared, Liverpool fans were certain another title was all but guaranteed. But football rarely unfolds on paper. Isak missed the entirety of preseason in what many describe as a self-imposed exile, arriving at Anfield rusty and unfit. The flawless team Liverpool had imagined started to show cracks, both with and without him on the pitch. Suddenly, Isak was expected not only to integrate seamlessly but to rescue a squad already facing unexpected challenges. The result has been a season under the microscope. Every missed chance, every lukewarm performance has intensified scrutiny. Rival fans delight in his struggles and even the patient Liverpool supporters are growing restless. The gap between expectation and reality has been stark, leaving the record signing's value under constant debate. Yet, there's a silver lining. Liverpool isn't entirely reliant on Isak. Hugo Ekitike, their other attacking weapon, has shown the capacity to terrorize defenses on his own, providing the Reds with the firepower they need while Isaac regains form. For now, Liverpool can continue to compete at the highest level, even if their marquee signing isn't yet living up to the hype. In football, patience is a virtue, but the real question is whether Isaac will soon justify every penny spent. Until then, Ekitike remains Liverpool's secret weapon, keeping the title hopes alive.

title: Take Off startup summit gathers global investors to Istanbul
transcription: Take off Istanbul is taking Turkish startups to the global stage. Hundreds of early stage teams, global investors and major tech players are packed under one roof, highlighting international cooperation and supporting emerging tech talent. And in the eighth iteration of the summit, more than 250 venture capitalists are meeting hundreds of industry newcomers. Whether you've just started out or you're already one of the big players, Takeoff has something to offer to the over 500 startups that gathered here. That can be a chance to connect directly with investors and customers or an opportunity to tap into fresh ideas, or sometimes to discover their next big partnership. Guiding young entrepreneurs as they establish themselves in the ecosystem is one of the core aims of the summit. And for many teams, this is where dreams meet opportunity. The head of Turkey's Investment and Finance office says the country's young talent is one of the main attractions for foreign investors. Investors know that Türkiye offers blue-collar workers, technical staff, engineers, software developers, senior managers, mid-level managers. So all levels of the talent is available in the country. So the investors who would like to utilize location and the talent availability of the country are, you know, choosing Türkiye. All these efforts are paying off. Türkiye's exports have been steadily rising, and in just 9 months, they've almost matched last year's total. Aerospace and defense systems top high-tech sales. And motor vehicles lead the list of medium to high-tech exports. As a result of these, you know, live and vibrant ecosystem, we have been attracting technology investments a lot in the post-covid era. Just a few numbers, you know, representing the first three quarters of this year, in the first nine months of this year, Türkiye attracted more than 11 billion dollars of investment, which means more than 40% increase in the FDI inflows. While many here look up to the homegrown successes, their journey is far from over. Takeoff is a snapshot of Türkiye's fast-growing tech ecosystem, and even the smallest booths here could be tomorrow's big breakthroughs. Sara Altash, TRT World, Istanbul.

title: First-Ever Footage: Killer Whales and Dolphins Hunt Together | Dalhousie University
transcription: So what we discovered was that uh two species, the resident killer whales and Pacific white-sided dolphins seem to be cooperatively foraging on uh salmon, and most likely adult chinook salmon off the coast of BC. So we think this is important for a couple of reasons. The first is that interspecies interactions are commonly observed um around the world. So we see whales and dolphins or different species of whales that interact with one another. But understanding the actual mechanism or the reason why we're seeing both species interacting has largely been speculative. And that's because a lot of the behaviors that are occurring are underwater and we just can't see what's going on. But then once we put the suction cup tags on the whales that had cameras and acoustic recorders, then we could actually see that not only were the killer whales following dolphins at the surface, but they would follow them to depth, down to around 60 m, where it would become really dark and we could just see the silhouettes of the dolphins at the head of the whale. And so what this told us was that the whales are, you know, working together to target uh large salmon for the killer whales to capture. It's important because if there's maybe another mechanism or a way to help facilitate um the resident killer whales to find their food, then that might be advantageous for the population. But we need to collect more data to try to figure out like, is this really prevalent? Like, how often are resident killer whales cooperatively foraging with Pacific white-sided dolphins? And that's something that we've yet to determine. To see that things were perhaps a bit more complex than we initially understood is is always exciting because like we just, you know, you scratch the surface with a lot of the research that you do, and then every now and then you get kind of lucky and something unexpected happens. And so this is one of those kind of lucky things.

Japan's government is assessing the extent of damage after this 7.5 magnitude earthquake struck North Japan earlier this week. The event was followed by multiple aftershocks and led officials to issue a warning of a possible megaquake to come in the area. Officials stress there's only about a 1% chance of a megaquake and the warning is just to encourage preparedness, but since there's a lot of chatter and misinformation online right now since that warning was issued, we want to clear things up. What is a megaquake and why is Japan at risk? Well, the friction from tectonic plates shifting against one another releases energy through the Earth's crust. We feel that as the ground shakes. That energy can also displace large amounts of ocean water that create tsunamis. Japan is surrounded by four tectonic plates, which make it vulnerable to earthquakes in general. The country experiences an average of 1500 a year, according to the University of Tokyo, but most of those quakes are very minor. Now, a megaquake has a magnitude of 8.0 or higher, which is 10 times stronger than a magnitude 7.0 quake. The 2011 quake that hit northern Japan was a 9.1, which along with its accompanying tsunami resulted in more than 19,000 deaths. If a megaquake happened in the area impacted by this week's earthquake, up to, you see the number right here, almost 200,000 lives could be lost and economic damage could reach almost 200 billion dollars according to government analysis. It could also cause a tsunami with a wave up to 98 ft tall. Now, it's important to stress that officials aren't saying a megaquake is imminent, but they are issuing this guidance as a warning of its possibility.

title: Jamie Carragher Slams Mohamed Salah: “A Disgrace” | Liverpool Drama Explained । USA TODAY NEWS
transcription: Jamie Carragher has finally broken his silence on the Mohamed Salah saga, calling the star's recent actions a disgrace. The Egyptian forward has sent shockwaves through Liverpool after claiming he's been thrown under the bus by the club. Salah has been left on the bench for the last three matches and didn't play a single minute in two of them, prompting questions about his future at Anfield. Following the 3-3 draw with Leeds, Salah claimed he had no relationship with manager Arne Slot and suggested that the weekend clash with Brighton could be his last for the club. Liverpool responded by leaving him out of the traveling squad for their upcoming Champions League fixture against Inter Milan, signaling a serious rift between player and club. Carragher, speaking on Sky Sports Monday Night Football, didn't hold back. He said Salah's post- Leeds comments were not just an emotional outburst, but a calculated move by him and his agent to maximize pressure on the club. Carragher reminded viewers that Salah had done something similar a year ago, playing on fans' emotions when Liverpool were top of the league. He suggested that now, after a poor result, Salah is once again trying to manipulate the narrative to his advantage, potentially undermining both the manager and the team. One line stood out to Carragher, thrown under the bus. He emphasized that Salah has twice in 12 months tried to throw the club under the bus, going after owners who have paid him handsomely for years and targeting the manager during a rough patch. Carragher argued that a player of Salah's caliber should be helping Liverpool in one of their worst runs of form since the 1950s, rather than creating off-field drama. The interview even went viral for a humorous moment when Carragher asked if he had ever criticized Salah on the pitch, only to be reminded by co-host David Jones that he had recently commented on Salah's legs. title: Ice hockey explained | A battle of warriors on ice 🏒
transcription: Fast action at breathtaking pace. Step into the world of ice hockey. Skaters are like warriors. They wear helmets, pads, and gloves for protection. Goalies, even more. They wear a mask, thicker pads, and extra body protection to absorb hard shots. Two teams play five skaters aside, which includes three forwards and two defensemen, fighting to put the puck past the opposing goaltender. The ice is divided into three zones, each with its own purpose. In the defensive zone, protect the net and prevent goals. You move through the neutral zone with quick passes and fast skating. Then fly into the attacking zone with the net as the target, setting up plays and taking hard shots to increase scoring chances. Break the rules and you go to the penalty box, usually for two minutes, sometimes four or even five. The team with a power play has more players on ice, using special strategies to create scoring chances. Games consist of three 20-minute periods. If scores are tied, an overtime period is played. Here, the first team to score wins. If no team scores, a shootout will decide the winner. Only in the gold medal game, teams play three on three overtime until a goal is scored. title: Adidas Men's Daily 4.0 Skate Shoes - Full Review
transcription: Let's take a look at these Adidas men's daily shoes and these are nothing fancy, just the way I like. They just look like a basic skate sneaker with a flat bottom and a wide rubber outsole. They come in a few color choices and these are the black, white, gum option. Even though they're really gray, not black. But they're not quite as basic on the inside as they appear at first. I've owned Vans and Converse Chuck Taylor All Stars and other similar shoes, so I'm definitely familiar with flat, unyielding slabs of rubber with a reinforced toe that's covered on top with a single layer of structure-free canvas. And these kind of look like that at first, but they're really not. They're actually super comfortable with a thick padded insole and the sides and top aren't just a single layer of canvas. They have some cushiness that feels really nice and padded. I'm recording this in the winter time, so I appreciate the fact that they actually have some insulation under my feet keeping the cold away from the ground below and around the sides and top from the air. The back heel area has an insert that keeps the structure upright and it won't fold like a lot of shoes in this category. And the canvas isn't as basic as you'd think. It feels like it has some kind of coating that provides some rigidity, and it makes them perhaps a little tougher and slightly less vulnerable to getting wet or dirty, but they're definitely not waterproof. Let's put these alongside a pair of Vans. Both are the same size 10 and a half. You can see the Adidas are just a little longer, but you don't really feel it much when you're wearing them because I think most of that length is coming from the padding in the back behind your Achilles and behind the heel. So it pushes your foot forward just a little more than the vans, which have nearly no padding at all in the back. And I'll also mention that they're a little bit wider and honestly, they're a lot more comfortable. But overall, these have been really surprising to me for how good they feel on my feet. And of course, I really like the way they look and I hope this short video has helped you decide whether to buy a pair of these Adidas men's daily shoes, and thanks for watching.

title: Pressure mounts on Indonesia to declare a national disaster after floods • FRANCE 24 English
transcription: Those displaced by floods are still fighting for their survival. Here in Western Sumatra, these rice farmers just escaped rising waters and deadly conditions as they were about to be swallowed up. Now they decry a lack of aid. To repair this house, to fix this road, that road, the river crossing, we're just left hanging if there's no assistance. We can't pass through, so where are we supposed to go? The torrential rains that fell on Sumatra cut access to many roads, complicating relief efforts. Several days after the start of the crisis, some isolated areas are now getting low on food and drinking water. The relief efforts are inadequate and the regency was not capable of handling this flood and landslide disaster alone. Though more than 1 million people have been displaced, the Indonesian government has so far ignored calls for a state of national disaster to be declared. Those demanding it say the measure would free up resources and improve the coordination of aid. Meanwhile, the government insists that crisis management is done by the provinces and that the 30 million US dollars in emergency funds should be enough, while also promising additional funding if needed. Indonesia has only declared a state of national disaster three times. First, during the 1992 earthquake, then in 2004 when a tsunami killed over 160,000 people, and finally during the COVID-19 pandemic. Some analysts are saying that the government is refusing to do so again to avoid any perception that it can't handle the crisis.

title: Luge explained | The fastest sport at the Winter Olympics  ✈️
transcription: Feet first, no brakes. Racing over 150 km an hour down the ice track. Step into the world of Luge, the fastest sport in the Winter Olympics. The way we push ourselves at the start can determine the race. We rock back and forth to accelerate forward. Then, paddle with spiked gloves to gain extra speed. From here on, we lie on our backs, feet stretched in an aerodynamic position to reduce drag. We steer with gentle pressure from our legs and shoulders. Steer too hard and we can lose speed. Steer too late, we can lose the line. When done right, we look still, even under 6Gs of pressure. There are five events at the Winter Olympic games. In men's and women's singles, it's one athlete, four runs, and the fastest total time wins. In men's and women's doubles, two athletes ride stacked with the heavier on top. We get two runs, and the team with the fastest total time wins. Team relays combine women's singles, men's doubles, men's singles, and women's doubles in one race, and in this order. Once we complete our leg of the race, we slap a pad at the bottom, triggering the gate to open for our teammates until all four sleds cross the finish line. We train for years to make the sport look effortless. See how fast we go at the Olympic Winter Games Milano Cortina 2026.
